contentBlocks.heading: How the Matching Actually Happens, Step by Step
contentBlocks.body:
A request starts with specifics, not a general enquiry: the language, the level (ab initio or Language B, Standard or Higher), the grade, and what is actually going wrong, whether that is weak oral confidence, a written paper that loses marks on register, or simply needing structured revision before May or November. IB Gram uses that to filter its tutor pool for people who teach that language at that level, not just anyone who happens to speak it.

A shortlist follows, usually more than one option, because fit matters as much as qualification. A tutor who is excellent with a nervous Grade 7 beginner is not automatically right for a Grade 12 student three months from a Higher Level oral. Parents can ask about a tutor's exam-board familiarity, teaching background and approach before committing to anything.

The first paid session is treated as a working diagnostic, not a sales pitch: current level against the criteria, gaps in vocabulary or structure, and the school's own internal deadlines for orals and written tasks, since these vary by school even within the same session year. From there, sessions run to a weekly plan with specific goals rather than open-ended revision. If a tutor is not the right match after a fair trial, IB Gram supports moving to another one, and this is treated as a normal part of finding fit, not a failure on either side.
items: Step 1: share language, level, grade and the actual problem
Step 2: receive a shortlist screened for that language and level
Step 3: first session works as a diagnostic against IB criteria
Step 4: weekly sessions run to specific, written goals
Step 5: switching tutors is supported if the fit is wrong

contentBlocks.heading: Where This Subject Sits, From MYP Phase 1 to the Diploma Exams
contentBlocks.body:
In the Middle Years Programme, language acquisition runs across six phases rather than grade-by-grade labels, so a Grade 8 student and a Grade 6 student might sit in the same phase, or a world apart, depending on when they started the language. Tutoring at this stage is about matching the phase honestly, not the grade on the timetable, because pushing a Phase 2 student into Phase 4 material teaches frustration, not language.

At Diploma level, the subject splits into ab initio, which is Standard Level only and built for genuine beginners, and Language B, offered at both Standard and Higher Level for students with some existing background in the language. The two are not interchangeable, and a student wrongly placed in Language B Higher Level with ab initio-level skills is set up for a hard two years.

Assessment follows criterion-related marking throughout, where command terms like analyse, discuss and justify carry specific weight that a generic language class does not teach, with academic honesty rules applying to any written coursework component just as they do in every other Diploma subject. The formal exams sit in the May and November sessions, but the pressure point most families underestimate is the internal deadline each school sets for its Individual Oral recording, which can land months before the written papers and is set independently by each school.
items: MYP Phases 1 to 6, matched by actual level, not grade
Ab initio: Standard Level only, for genuine beginners
Language B: Standard or Higher Level, some background required
Command-term literacy: analyse, discuss, justify, evaluate
May and November exam sessions; internal oral deadlines set by each school

contentBlocks.heading: Online, Home or Both, What a Language Subject Actually Needs
contentBlocks.body:
Online tutoring is the default for this subject for one plain reason: the tutor a student needs, someone fluent, IB-familiar, and available at the right level and time, is unlikely to live in the same neighbourhood. Video sessions handle conversation practice, listening comprehension and oral rehearsal reasonably well, and recordings can be reviewed afterward, which a live-only home session cannot offer.

Home tutoring still has a place, particularly for a younger MYP student who benefits from someone physically present to hold attention and manage a session without a screen in the way. It depends entirely on whether a tutor happens to be within a workable travel radius, and for less commonly taught languages, that radius is often the honest limitation: a home tutor for German or Mandarin at the right level simply may not exist within reasonable travelling distance, whereas one is far easier to find online.

Hybrid plans are the practical middle path many families settle on: online sessions for the bulk of weekly work, with occasional home sessions timed around a mock exam or before a school's internal oral deadline, when in-person feedback on delivery and body language adds something a screen cannot fully replicate. Which mix works best depends on the language, the student's age and the family's own schedule, and it can change over the course of a year rather than being fixed from day one.
items: Online: best default for rarer languages and specialist tutors
Home: suits younger MYP students who need someone present
Hybrid: online through the term, home before an oral or mock
Honest limit: home availability depends on tutor location, not preference

contentBlocks.heading: Reading, Listening, Writing and the Individual Oral, What Each Skill Needs
contentBlocks.body:
IB Language Acquisition tests four distinct skills, and a tutor who is strong in one is not automatically strong in all four. The receptive paper covers reading and listening comprehension across a range of text types, from adverts and blogs to more formal correspondence, and it rewards a student who can infer meaning without knowing every word, a skill that has to be practised deliberately, not absorbed by osmosis.

The productive paper asks students to write for a specific audience and purpose, at ab initio and Standard Level, and at Higher Level to also respond to a literary or non-literary text, which trips up strong conversational speakers who have never structured a formal opinion essay in the target language before.

The Individual Oral carries real weight and often causes the most anxiety, because it is recorded, assessed against specific criteria around interaction and language range, and scheduled internally by the school, which means the true deadline is rarely the one printed in the general exam calendar. Vocabulary breadth and grammatical accuracy matter, but so does something harder to coach quickly: comfort improvising in the language under mild pressure, which is exactly what regular tutor-led conversation practice is meant to build over weeks, not in a single cram session the night before an exam.
items: Receptive skills: reading and listening across varied text types
Productive skills: writing for audience and purpose at every level
Individual Oral: interaction, language range, scheduled by the school
Ab initio and Standard Level add a literary or non-literary response
Vocabulary and structure matter less than comfort improvising live

contentBlocks.heading: Where the School's Own Teacher Fits Into This
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform. It is not affiliated with the IB Organization, Cambridge International or Pearson Edexcel, and no tutor matched through it claims to represent a student's school. That distinction matters more in a language subject than most, because every IB World School builds its own scheme of work, sets its own pace through the syllabus, and picks its own internal deadline for the Individual Oral, and a tutor working blind to that schedule is not actually helping.

A useful tutor works from the same command terms, the same mark scheme language and the same assessment criteria the school's own teacher already uses, rather than introducing a competing method. Group 2 classes are also often mixed, with ab initio, Standard Level and Higher Level students technically taught together depending on how a school timetables its options, and a teacher managing fifteen or more students at different points in the syllabus cannot give any one of them sustained one-to-one correction time on pronunciation, register or written structure. That is the actual gap tutoring fills, not replacing the classroom teacher, but giving a student the individual attention a mixed-level class structurally cannot provide, coordinated around the same deadlines and criteria the school has already set.
items: IB Gram is independent, no affiliation with the IB Organization
Tutors align to the student's own school scheme, not a competing one
Mixed-level Group 2 classes limit individual correction time
Coordination around the school's own internal oral and coursework deadlines

contentBlocks.heading: The Same Problem, From One City to the Next
contentBlocks.body:
A family in Chandigarh searching for an ab initio French tutor runs into the same wall as a family in Bhubaneswar looking for Mandarin B at Higher Level: the specialist they need rarely lives nearby. Cities such as Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Chennai, Coimbatore, Dehradun, Delhi, Faridabad, Ghaziabad and Greater Noida all show the identical pattern, plenty of general tutors, far fewer who teach a specific IB language at a specific level and know the syllabus well enough to be useful in week one rather than week six.

Online matching removes the geography constraint from that search entirely. A tutor does not need to live in Bhopal to teach a Bhopal-based Grade 10 student Language B German at Higher Level; they need to be strong in the language, familiar with the criteria, and available at a time that works for both households. That is precisely where the worldwide, time-zone-first model earns its keep, because IB families are not clustered in one place. They are spread across cities and countries, often without another IB Diploma cohort nearby to draw a local tutor pool from.

Home tutoring remains an option in any of these cities, but it is the exception rather than the plan, and it depends on a tutor's own travel route lining up with the family's area, which is worth checking honestly before assuming it, rather than after a session has already been booked.

Online matching removes the local-availability bottleneck entirely
Home tutoring depends on a tutor's own travel route, checked case by case
Works the same way for a family in any time zone, not only these cities

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before Anyone Is Matched
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor's own claim to speak a language fluently is the least useful signal a parent can rely on. Before a match is made, IB Gram looks at whether a tutor has actual teaching experience with that specific language at the level requested, since ab initio beginners need a different skill from coaching a Higher Level oral, along with familiarity with IB assessment criteria and command terms, because teaching a language generally and teaching it against IB's specific mark schemes are not the same job.

Subject-matter background is checked against the language and level being requested, not assumed from a general profile. A tutor who teaches Language B French at Standard Level well is not automatically the right fit for ab initio Mandarin at Higher Level, since these are different skills bundled under one subject name, and matching treats them as such rather than defaulting to whoever is available first.

None of this produces a guarantee, and it should not be sold as one. What it produces is a tutor whose background genuinely fits the request, an honest starting point rather than an inflated one, and a process a parent can ask questions about before committing: which language and level combinations a tutor actually teaches, how long they have taught that specific course, and whether they have handled the Individual Oral component before, since that is where much of the marking-scheme nuance actually lives.
items: Teaching experience checked against the specific language and level
Familiarity with IB command terms and criterion-related marking
No blanket profiles, ab initio and Higher Level treated as different skills
Parents can ask what a tutor has actually taught before, and for how long

contentBlocks.heading: What a Parent Should Actually See by Week Four
contentBlocks.body:
The first session should produce more than a friendly introduction. It should surface a genuine read on where the student stands against IB criteria, not a vague sense that things are fine, along with a look at the school's own internal deadlines, since these often sit earlier than families expect and get missed by tutoring plans built around the general exam calendar instead of the actual school one. A written note of the plan for the coming weeks, even a short one, is a reasonable thing to ask for.

By around week four, the visible signal is usually behavioural before it is score-based: a student attempting to speak or write without translating word-for-word in their head first, catching their own register mistakes before a tutor points them out, or approaching a past-paper question with a plan instead of a blank stare. These are not guarantees of a particular grade, and nobody honest promises one this early, or ever, since so much depends on where a student started and how much practice happens outside sessions too.

If none of that is visible by week four, that is useful information, not a reason to wait quietly for another month. It is a fair point to raise directly, and a fair point at which to ask whether the tutor is still the right match for this particular student, or whether the pace or teaching style needs to change before more weeks are spent on the wrong approach.
items: Session one: honest diagnostic against IB criteria, not small talk
School's internal deadlines checked against the general exam calendar
Week four: fewer word-for-word translations, more self-caught errors
No score guarantees, progress is described, not promised, this early

contentBlocks.heading: Start With the Language and Level, Not a General Enquiry
contentBlocks.body:
Most families lose time at the start by describing the problem too broadly, something like needs a language tutor, when the useful starting point is specific: which language, ab initio or Language B, Standard or Higher Level, which grade, and what the actual sticking point is. That single change turns a slow, generic search into a short, relevant shortlist.

From there, IB Gram can match against tutors who teach that exact combination, check their familiarity with the school's own assessment style, and set up a first session that is diagnostic rather than exploratory. This depends on level and language, and is subject to tutor availability at the time, but it is treated as a starting conversation, not a locked-in commitment. A trial session that does not fit is a normal outcome, not a wasted one, and switching from there is straightforward.

For a family weighing online against home tutoring, or unsure whether ab initio or Language B is the right fit for where a student actually is, that is exactly the kind of question worth raising before the first session is booked, rather than worked out afterward through trial and error alone. Fees and scheduling depend on the tutor matched and the plan agreed, and both are discussed plainly before anything is confirmed.
items: Start with language, level and grade, not a general request
First session is diagnostic, not a sales conversation
Switching tutors after a trial is normal, not a failure
Fees and scheduling depend on the tutor matched, discussed upfront

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work for a language subject, or is in-person better?
faqs.answer: For most students, yes. Video calls handle conversation practice, listening comprehension and oral rehearsal well, and sessions can be recorded for review afterward, which an in-person-only session cannot offer. Online also opens up tutors who teach the exact language and level needed, rather than whoever happens to live nearby. In-person still helps some younger learners stay focused, and can be useful around an oral exam for feedback on delivery and body language. Which works better depends on the student's age, the language, and how self-directed they are during a video call.

faqs.question: What's the actual difference between Language Acquisition and Language A?
faqs.answer: Language A is for a student's best language, usually studied through literature and built for near-native fluency. Language Acquisition, ab initio or Language B, is for learning a language that is not a student's strongest, at a beginner or intermediate-to-advanced level depending on the course. A parent search sometimes lands on a Language A literature tutor by mistake, which is a poor fit for a student who actually needs grammar, vocabulary and oral confidence built from a lower base.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Individual Oral if I don't speak the language myself to check their work?
faqs.answer: That's fine, a parent isn't expected to assess the language content directly. What is worth checking instead is whether the tutor has taught that specific IB course before and can explain, in plain terms, how the Individual Oral is marked and what the student is being asked to improve after each practice run. Ask for a short summary after sessions: what was worked on, what still needs attention. That gives visibility into progress without needing to judge the language yourself.

faqs.question: How much does IB Language Acquisition tutoring cost?
faqs.answer: Fees vary by tutor, language, level and how often sessions run, and are agreed directly once a match is made rather than fixed platform-wide. A rarer language or Higher Level oral coaching close to an exam session can cost more than routine weekly Standard Level support. It is reasonable to ask for the rate and what a session actually covers before committing, and to compare more than one shortlisted tutor before choosing.

faqs.question: What if the tutor turns out to be the wrong fit for my child?
faqs.answer: It happens, and it is treated as a normal part of finding fit rather than a problem to push through. If a trial session or the first few weeks show a mismatch in teaching style, pace or personality, IB Gram supports moving to another tutor from the shortlist. It helps to say specifically what wasn't working, too fast, too passive, not enough oral practice, so the next match addresses it directly rather than repeating the same issue.

faqs.question: Is home tutoring available, or is it online only?
faqs.answer: Both exist, but home tutoring depends on whether a suitably qualified tutor for that specific language and level happens to be within a workable travel distance, and it is not guaranteed in every city or every language. Online is the more reliable default, especially for less commonly taught languages where a local specialist may simply not exist nearby. Hybrid plans, mixing online sessions with occasional home visits, are also possible depending on tutor availability.

faqs.question: My child is starting Language B in Grade 11, later than most classmates. Is it too late to catch up?
faqs.answer: It's tighter, not impossible, and the honest answer depends on the starting level and how much time is realistically available outside school. Standard Level has more room to build up over two years than Higher Level does. A late start usually means prioritising ruthlessly, strong Individual Oral technique and solid writing structure first, breadth of vocabulary second, rather than trying to cover everything evenly the way a student who started in Grade 9 could.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work through past papers with my child?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it's a normal part of most tutoring plans closer to the May or November session, going through past reading and listening comprehension papers, reviewing mark schemes together, and identifying where marks are being lost on structure rather than language ability alone. It works best once a student has covered the relevant vocabulary and grammar; starting past papers too early, before the basics are solid, tends to be discouraging rather than useful.

faqs.question: Do you have tutors for less commonly taught languages, or mainly French and Spanish?
faqs.answer: Availability depends on the specific language and level requested, and is checked at the time of matching rather than promised in advance. Widely taught languages like French, Spanish and German tend to have a deeper pool, while a less common language may take longer to match or be more realistically found online than through home tutoring. It's worth asking directly during matching rather than assuming either way.

faqs.question: How does scheduling work if I'm in a very different time zone from most tutors?
faqs.answer: Sessions are arranged around the family's own time zone from the start, not the tutor's, since IB Gram works with tutors across many time zones already. A family in Dehradun or Greater Noida and a family several time zones away are handled the same way: availability is matched to when the student can realistically attend consistently, including around school hours and exam-season fatigue, rather than to whichever tutor happens to be online at a convenient moment.

heroTitle: IB Math AA HL Tutors, Matched to Your Syllabus Level
heroSubtitle: A tutor who has actually taught the AA HL syllabus at Paper 3 level, not a generalist covering three subjects. Matching considers your grade, your school's IA deadlines, and whether you sit the May or November session, then sets up online, home or hybrid sessions accordingly.
introSummary: Parents searching for IB Math AA HL tutors are usually trying to fix one of two problems: a student who has fallen behind on Paper 1 and Paper 2 technique, or one who understands the content but loses marks on command terms and mark-scheme wording. IB Math AA HL is the hardest of the IB maths pathways, built for students continuing to mathematics-heavy degrees, and it rewards structured practice more than raw ability. IB Gram matches families with tutors who teach this exact syllabus online worldwide, or through home and hybrid options where a tutor is local.

contentBlocks.heading: What Actually Moves an AA HL Grade
contentBlocks.body: Most searches for an IB Math AA HL tutor start with a symptom: a mock result lower than the school predicted, a topic like vectors or complex numbers that never clicked, or a feeling that revision is not converting into marks. The instinct is to look for the tutor with the loudest claims. That is rarely the fix. AA HL rewards technique as much as understanding — knowing which command term a question is using, how a mark scheme awards method marks even when the final answer is wrong, and how to allocate time across Paper 1 (no calculator), Paper 2 (calculator) and Paper 3 (extended problem-solving). A tutor who has taught this exact syllabus, not just A-level or a generic maths-tutor background, can see these patterns immediately. So the first question worth asking is not whether a tutor is good at maths but whether they have taught AA HL through to an actual May or November session. IB Gram's matching starts from that question rather than from a generic subject label. A student six months from exams needs someone who can triage weak topics fast. A student in Grade 6 or 7 building early number and algebra foundations needs a completely different pace and personality. Both are IB Math AA HL tutoring in name; in practice, they are different jobs, and treating them the same is where a lot of tutoring spend gets wasted.
items: Weak topics and weak technique are different problems
Paper 1, 2 and 3 need separate practice, not just more of the same
Command terms and mark-scheme wording cost marks even with the right answer
Pace differs hugely between Grade 6 foundations and Grade 12 exam finishing

contentBlocks.heading: Where the Marks Are Lost in the AA HL Syllabus
contentBlocks.body: AA HL sits alongside AA SL and AI HL/SL in the IB's maths pathways, but it is the version built for students planning engineering, physics, computer science or economics degrees that assume calculus fluency. The syllabus load is heavy: functions, sequences and series, trigonometry and complex numbers in the earlier stages, then differential calculus, integration, vectors, and an optional extension topic depending on the school's chosen option. Paper 3, unique to HL, is where a lot of otherwise strong students underperform — it asks for sustained problem-solving across multiple parts of a single question, not the shorter discrete questions of Papers 1 and 2. Internal assessment adds a second, separate pressure: a mathematical exploration marked against criteria that reward mathematical communication and personal engagement, not just correct working. A tutor who only drills Paper 1 and 2 style questions will leave a student under-prepared for Paper 3's demands and for an IA that needs an original angle. Good AA HL tutoring treats these as three distinct skills to build in parallel rather than one undifferentiated maths-help block, and adjusts the balance depending on how far out the exam session is and which topics the school has already covered. None of this is optional polish; it is where the actual marks in a real paper sit, and skipping it to cover more content faster tends to backfire in the exam room.
items: Functions, calculus, vectors and complex numbers form the core load
Paper 3 needs sustained multi-part problem-solving, not quick-fire questions
The IA exploration is marked on communication and engagement, not just correct answers
Option topic choice depends on what the school has already taught

contentBlocks.heading: How a Tutor Gets Matched to Your Child
contentBlocks.body: Matching starts with three things: current grade or year group, the exam session being targeted, and what has actually been covered in school so far, since schools sequence AA HL topics differently. A family shares these details, and IB Gram shortlists tutors whose subject background and experience fit — someone who has taught AA HL through to Paper 3 and IA supervision for a Grade 11 or 12 student, or someone comfortable building early calculus and algebra fluency for a younger student in Grade 6 to 9. A short introductory call or first session follows, where the tutor and family can both check fit before committing to a term of sessions. This step matters more than it sounds: a tutor who is excellent for a self-directed Grade 12 student chasing one specific paper weakness may be the wrong personality for a Grade 7 student who needs more encouragement and slower pacing. If the first match is not right, IB Gram looks again rather than expecting a family to make it work. Ongoing sessions are reviewed against a simple standard: is the student's confidence and accuracy on practice questions improving over four to six weeks, not just whether the sessions are pleasant. Weekly goals are set collaboratively so progress is visible rather than assumed, and the plan is adjusted if a mock or school assessment shows a gap the current plan is not closing.
items: Grade, exam session and syllabus coverage set the starting shortlist
First session is a two-way fit check, not a locked-in commitment
Weekly goals make progress checkable, not just felt
Plan is adjusted after mocks or school assessments, not left on autopilot

contentBlocks.heading: Where Home Sessions Can Be Arranged
contentBlocks.body: Online IB Math AA HL tutoring is available everywhere, in the family's own time zone, and does not depend on which city a tutor happens to live in — this is the option most AA HL families end up using, since specialist HL-level tutors are not evenly spread across every city. Home tutoring is different: it depends on a tutor actually being available to travel in that city, so coverage varies. IB Gram has tutors who take home sessions in cities including Delhi, Bangalore, Chennai, Ahmedabad, Chandigarh, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Coimbatore, Dehradun, Faridabad, Ghaziabad and Greater Noida, though availability in any one of these at a given time depends on which tutors are currently taking new students there. If a family is in one of these cities and wants an in-person option, that can be checked directly; if not, or if the nearest available tutor is not a strong subject match, online is usually the better route rather than compromising on subject depth for the sake of a home visit. A hybrid setup — mostly online with an occasional in-person session, for instance before a mock or exam — is workable in most of these cities too, and tends to suit older HL students better than very young learners, who generally benefit from more consistent in-person contact early on.
items: Online works from any of these cities and beyond, same time zone as the family
Home sessions depend on tutor availability city by city, not guaranteed
Cities with home coverage include Delhi, Bangalore, Chennai and others listed above
Hybrid suits older HL students better than very young learners

contentBlocks.heading: Grade 6 to Grade 12: What Changes Along the Way
contentBlocks.body: IB Gram supports Math AA HL-track students from Grade 6 through Grade 12, though what tutoring means changes a lot across that range. In Grade 6 to 8, the actual IB Diploma subject has not started yet — this is about building the algebra, number sense and problem-solving habits that make AA HL survivable later, particularly for a student likely to choose the HL pathway rather than SL or AI. From Grade 9 to 10, in the MYP years at most schools, the focus shifts to closing specific gaps before DP options are chosen, since a shaky foundation in functions or trigonometry at this stage tends to resurface directly in AA HL Paper 1. Grade 11 and 12 is the Diploma proper: two years of new content, an IA due partway through, and mocks used by the school to predict grades before the real exam session. A tutor working with a Grade 11 student in October needs a different plan than one working with the same student in March of Grade 12, closer to exams, when the priority shifts almost entirely to timed practice and error patterns rather than new content. Starting AA HL support late, in the final months before exams, narrows what is realistically achievable — it can still help, but it will not undo two years of gaps, and an honest tutor will say so rather than promise otherwise.
items: Grade 6-8: algebra and number-sense foundations before HL formally starts
Grade 9-10: closing gaps before DP subject and level choices are locked in
Grade 11-12: new content, IA, mocks, then timed exam practice
Starting in the final months limits, but does not eliminate, what can improve

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Tutor Is Introduced
contentBlocks.body: Every tutor on IB Gram is reviewed for subject background and relevant teaching experience before being introduced to a family — specifically, whether they have taught AA HL content at the level being requested, not just mathematics in general. For Grade 11-12 matches, that includes checking familiarity with IA supervision, since guiding a mathematical exploration without steering it into academic honesty problems is a specific skill, distinct from teaching content. IB tutoring more broadly has to work within concept-based learning and the IB's command-term language, and a tutor unfamiliar with how these are used in AA HL mark schemes will teach technically correct maths that still loses marks in the actual exam. Background and subject experience are reviewed as part of this process; families can ask what a specific tutor's experience with AA HL has been before committing to sessions, and that information is available on request rather than hidden behind marketing copy. What IB Gram does not do is promise a grade outcome, publish a tutor count, or claim any relationship with the IB Organization — this is a matching platform, not an examination body, and responsibility for exam results sits with the student's own work and the school's assessment. What can be described honestly is the process: how a match is made, what is checked beforehand, and what a first month of sessions should show if the match is working.
items: Subject background checked against the specific level being requested
IA supervision experience checked separately for Grade 11-12 matches
Familiarity with command terms and AA HL mark schemes, not generic maths teaching
No affiliation with the IB Organization; no promised grade outcomes

contentBlocks.heading: Online, Home or Hybrid: The Honest Trade-offs
contentBlocks.body: Online tutoring is the default recommendation for most AA HL families, and not for a lack of better options — it simply gives access to a specialist HL-level tutor regardless of which city they live in, which matters more for a demanding subject like AA HL than for a subject where any competent generalist will do. Screen-sharing a graphing tool or working through a past paper together over video covers most topics, including Paper 3-style extended questions. Home tutoring has real advantages for younger students, particularly Grade 6 to 9, who often concentrate better with someone physically present and benefit from a fixed weekly routine that does not depend on a laptop and stable internet. It also suits families who specifically want in-person accountability for a student who tends to drift during online sessions. The trade-off is availability: a strong home tutor has to already be reachable in that part of the city, and traffic or distance can quietly cap how often sessions actually happen even when they are scheduled weekly. Hybrid plans try to take the better half of both — regular online sessions for content and practice, with occasional in-person sessions timed around mocks or exam weeks, when working through a full timed paper together in the same room adds something a screen cannot. None of these three is objectively best; the right one depends on the student's age, attention style and how reliably a tutor can actually be reached.
items: Online: access to specialist HL tutors, works from any city
Home: better for younger students who need in-person routine and focus
Hybrid: online for regular practice, in-person around mocks and exam prep
Home tutoring's real limit is travel and tutor availability, not willingness

contentBlocks.heading: Every School Sets Its Own IA and Mock Calendar
contentBlocks.body: One detail catches families off guard: there is no single AA HL calendar. The IB Organization sets the May and November examination sessions, but internal assessment deadlines, mock exam dates, and how much of the syllabus is covered before mocks are all decided by the individual school. This means two students in the same grade, both doing AA HL, can be at meaningfully different points in the syllabus at the same time of year — one may already have sat a full mock under Paper 3 conditions, another may not have touched the option topic yet. A tutor needs to know a student's actual school-set timeline, not a generic IB calendar, before building a study plan; a plan built around the wrong assumed deadline can leave a student unprepared for their real mock or IA submission date. IB Gram works from whatever timeline the family and school have actually set, and asks for this directly during matching rather than assuming a standard schedule. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and has no affiliation with the IB Organization, Cambridge International, Pearson Edexcel, or with any individual school — it does not have access to a school's internal calendar beyond what the family shares, so keeping a tutor updated on school-specific deadlines is the family's role, not something assumed automatically.
items: May and November are IB-wide; IA deadlines and mocks are set by each school
Two same-grade AA HL students can be at different syllabus points
Study plans should follow the actual school timeline, not a generic one
IB Gram is independent, with no affiliation to the IB Organization or any school

contentBlocks.heading: What We Don't Promise, and What We Do
contentBlocks.body: No tutor on IB Gram is presented with a guaranteed grade, a specific score improvement, or a published success rate — anyone claiming this for AA HL, one of the harder HL subjects to forecast, is not being straight with you. What can be offered instead is a clear, checkable process. A first session should cover a genuine diagnostic: which topics are solid, which are shaky, and what the actual gap is between current performance and the target grade, based on real practice questions rather than a general conversation about confidence. By the end of the first month, a parent should be able to see specific things — which topics moved from shaky to solid, how timing on a full paper has changed, and whether the student's own error log shows fewer repeated mistakes. If none of that is visible after a reasonable stretch of sessions, that is a signal to review the match, not to simply continue and hope it improves on its own. Switching tutors mid-term is possible and, when the fit genuinely is not working, usually the right call rather than a failure to be avoided — a wrong-fit tutor rarely turns into a right one just from more sessions. Availability for any given tutor, subject level or time slot depends on current demand and cannot be promised in advance of an actual match being made.
items: No guaranteed grades or invented success statistics, ever
First session is a real diagnostic against practice questions
Four-week check: topics moved, timing improved, fewer repeated errors
Switching tutors mid-term is normal when a match genuinely is not working

contentBlocks.heading: Starting This Week, Wherever You Are
contentBlocks.body: There is no ideal week to start AA HL tutoring — a student six weeks from a mock and a student in Grade 7 building foundations both benefit from starting now rather than waiting for a better moment, since the gap that prompted the search rarely closes on its own. The process itself is short: share the current grade, the target exam session, and what has already been covered, and a shortlist of matching tutors follows, ready for online sessions in the family's own time zone or, subject to availability, home and hybrid options in cities where a tutor is reachable. From there, the first session is a diagnostic rather than a sales pitch, and the plan that follows is built around the actual gap it finds, not a generic AA HL syllabus. Families anywhere with an IB-affiliated school can start from the same first step — the exam session might be May or November, the student might be in Grade 6 or in a final year of Grade 12; the starting move does not change. What follows after that first session — how weekly goals are set, how progress is checked at four weeks, whether the tutor is a genuine fit for this particular student — is where the actual value of the match shows up or does not, and IB Gram treats that as the real test, not the sign-up itself.
items: Start point is the same regardless of grade or exam session: share the gap, get a shortlist
First session diagnoses before any plan is built
Online now, home or hybrid where a tutor is available and reachable
Real test is week four progress, not the sign-up

faqs.question: How is IB Math AA HL different from AI HL, and does that change what a tutor should focus on?
faqs.answer: AA HL assumes calculus fluency and pure mathematical reasoning, including proof, while AI HL leans toward applied and technology-based problem-solving with more modelling and statistics. A tutor who has only taught AI HL will not automatically transfer well to AA HL's Paper 3, which demands sustained algebraic manipulation rather than calculator-assisted modelling. If your child switched from AI to AA, or is deciding between them, say so during matching — the tutor's own background in one pathway versus the other genuinely matters, more than general teaching experience does.

faqs.question: Can online tutoring actually work for a subject this demanding, or does AA HL need in-person teaching?
faqs.answer: For most students, yes. Screen-sharing lets a tutor work through the same graph, diagram or worked solution in real time, which covers most of what AA HL needs, including Paper 3-style multi-part questions. Where online genuinely struggles is with very young students who lose focus without someone physically present, or a student who needs frequent, informal checking-in rather than a scheduled session. For most Grade 10-12 AA HL students, online is not a compromise; it is usually how the strongest available subject match is reached in the first place.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor and my child just don't click?
faqs.answer: This does happen, and it is not something to push through for the sake of consistency. Tell IB Gram what specifically was not working — pace, teaching style, personality — and a different tutor can be matched using that information, rather than starting the whole search again from scratch. A wrong-fit tutor rarely improves the situation with more sessions; the earlier a mismatch is flagged, the less time and momentum is lost before exams or an IA deadline.

faqs.question: How much does IB Math AA HL tutoring cost?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the tutor's experience level, whether sessions are online, home or hybrid, and how many sessions are booked per week, so there is no single number that applies to every family. Home tutoring in most cities costs more than online, largely because of travel time. The clearest way to get an accurate figure is to go through matching with your actual details — grade, session target, mode — since a quote based on generic assumptions is not reliable.

faqs.question: My child is behind on Paper 3 specifically. Can a tutor focus on just that?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is a common, specific request. Paper 3 tests sustained problem-solving across a single extended question rather than shorter discrete ones, so improving on it often means practising full past-paper Paper 3 questions under timed conditions and reviewing the mark scheme's method-mark structure afterward, rather than more general topic revision. A tutor can build a plan around Paper 3 alone for a few weeks if that is genuinely the gap, rather than defaulting to a generic all-topics revision course.

faqs.question: Is home tutoring available in my city?
faqs.answer: It depends on tutor availability at the time you ask — IB Gram currently has tutors taking home sessions in cities including Delhi, Bangalore, Chennai, Ahmedabad, Chandigarh, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Coimbatore, Dehradun, Faridabad, Ghaziabad and Greater Noida, but coverage within any of these cities varies by area and by which tutors are free at a given time. If home tutoring is not available where you are, or the nearest tutor is not the strongest subject match, online tutoring in your own time zone is usually the better choice.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the mathematical exploration (IA) as well as exam content?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the two need different handling. IA supervision means helping a student choose a genuinely personal topic, structure the exploration against the assessment criteria, and stay within academic honesty rules — a tutor should guide the mathematical thinking, not write or heavily rewrite the exploration itself. If your child needs IA help, mention it during matching, since not every AA HL tutor has supervised explorations before, and this is worth checking rather than assuming.

faqs.question: What if my child starts tutoring only a few months before the exam?
faqs.answer: It can still help, but it will not fully undo two years of gaps, and any tutor telling you otherwise is overselling. In the final months, the honest priority is timed past-paper practice, a focused error log, and shoring up the two or three topics costing the most marks, rather than trying to re-teach the entire syllabus. Starting late narrows what is achievable; it does not make tutoring pointless, and a realistic plan built around the actual time left tends to outperform a generic full-syllabus one.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram guarantee a grade improvement?
faqs.answer: No, and treat any platform that does with suspicion — grade outcomes depend on the student's own work, the school's teaching and assessment, and factors no tutor fully controls. What can be described honestly is the process: how tutors are matched to a student's actual level and gap, what a first session diagnoses, and what should be visible by week four. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with the IB Organization, and does not publish invented statistics or guaranteed results.

faqs.question: What ages or grades does this cover — is it only for Grade 11-12 Diploma students?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram supports AA HL-track students from Grade 6 through Grade 12. Younger students, Grade 6 to 8, typically work on the algebra and number-sense foundations that make AA HL manageable later, rather than AA HL content itself, which formally starts in Grade 11. Grade 9-10 tutoring usually focuses on closing gaps before DP subject choices are locked in. The right starting point depends on the student's current grade and school timeline, not a fixed age cutoff.

introSummary: Looking for IB Math AI HL tutors usually means one of three things: term work is falling behind, the IA is stuck, or a mock result was worse than expected. IB Gram matches families with tutors who teach Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level specifically, not a Math generalist reading the syllabus for the first time, for students from Grade 6 through Grade 12. Lessons run online worldwide in your own time zone; home tutoring depends on a tutor's availability in your city, and hybrid plans combine both across the May and November examination sessions.

contentBlocks.heading: Where Your Child Sits in the IB Math AI HL Calendar
contentBlocks.body: IB Math AI HL runs on two fixed points a year: the May and November examination sessions. Everything else, internal assessment deadlines, mock exams, the pace of new topics, is set by the individual school around those two dates, which means the honest first question is not 'do you need a tutor' but 'what is due next, and when.' A student in Grade 11 whose school has scheduled the IA draft for six weeks from now needs different help than a Grade 12 student two months from finals with three papers still shaky. Starting IB Math AI HL tutoring in the term before a mock is common and useful: there is time to close gaps in statistics, financial mathematics or discrete topics that AI HL leans on more than AA. Starting it the month before a final paper is still worth doing, but it should be pitched as exam technique and mark-scheme drilling, not fresh teaching of unfamiliar content; a tutor who promises otherwise is overselling what four or five sessions can do. Grade 6 to Grade 8 students preparing for a later HL choice benefit from a different kind of session: building number fluency and modelling habits early, well before command terms and criterion-related grading become the daily language of class. Whichever stage a family is at, the useful question to ask on a first call is simple: what result is the school actually expecting by the next reporting date, and how many sessions realistically get there.

November session: alternative cohort and resit window

contentBlocks.heading: Online, Home or a Mix — What Actually Fits AI HL
contentBlocks.body: AI HL sessions lean on technology more than most IB Math tutoring, because the syllabus assumes a graphic display calculator and comfortable spreadsheet work throughout, which changes what 'online' should mean here. A tutor sharing a screen, working through a GDC function step by step with the student mirroring on their own device, often teaches AI HL techniques better than a home tutor writing on paper at a kitchen table, because the exam itself rewards calculator fluency in Papers 1 and 2. Online is not automatically the right call for every student, though. A Grade 6 or 7 student building early number and modelling habits, or a student who has struggled to stay focused on video calls before, may do better face to face, and home tutoring remains available depending on a tutor's location and travel range. Hybrid plans exist for a reason: a family might keep weekly online sessions for steady pace and content coverage, then add an occasional in-person session before a mock or ahead of the IA deadline, when working through a printed draft together is simply easier than a shared document. None of the three modes is inherently better; the honest answer depends on the student's age, how self-directed they already are, and whether a suitable tutor happens to be reachable in person at all. Online removes that last constraint entirely and opens up specialist AI HL tutors regardless of where the family is based.
items: Online: screen-shared GDC work, any time zone
Home: depends on tutor travel range and availability
Hybrid: weekly online plus occasional in-person sessions
Best online fit: self-directed students from Grade 9 up
Best home fit: younger learners, Grade 6-8

contentBlocks.heading: What AI HL Actually Demands, Beyond the Formula List
contentBlocks.body: IB Math AI HL is built around applying mathematics to real, often messy contexts: modelling, statistics, financial mathematics and technology-driven problem solving carry more weight here than in Analysis and Approaches, where proof and pure technique dominate. That distinction matters for tutoring because a tutor strong in AA HL is not automatically strong in AI HL; the two courses reward different instincts, and a family switching a tutor from one to the other mid-year should expect an adjustment period. Command terms do a lot of quiet work in IB Math: 'justify', 'hence', 'sketch' and 'show that' each demand a specific kind of answer, and a large share of lost marks in mock papers comes from students who know the mathematics but answer the wrong command term. A tutor's job during exam-paper preparation is as much about training that response as it is about content. Academic honesty applies directly to the internal assessment, the mathematical exploration, where a tutor can guide structure, questioning and technique but the mathematical thinking and write-up have to be the student's own; a good tutor is explicit about that line rather than blurring it. Assessment is criterion-related rather than purely mark-total based, which means a student can improve a specific criterion, such as communication or use of technology, without necessarily rewriting the whole exploration, and a tutor who understands the criteria can target revisions precisely instead of asking for a full redraft.

Command-term accuracy costs marks as often as content gaps do
IA (exploration) built on the student's own mathematical thinking

GDC and spreadsheet fluency assumed throughout

contentBlocks.heading: Families Logging In From Very Different Places
contentBlocks.body: IB Gram's Math AI HL tutoring is not tied to one office or one time zone; a family logging in from Ahmedabad, Bangalore or Chennai sits in the same booking system as one logging in from Dehradun, Faridabad or Greater Noida, each getting a session scheduled around their own school day rather than a tutor's. That range is the point: an AI HL specialist is a narrower pool than a general Math tutor, and confining the search to whoever happens to live nearby usually means settling for a generalist. Online removes that ceiling. A student in Chandigarh preparing for a November session and a student in Coimbatore preparing for May can both be matched on subject depth and current syllabus fit rather than geography. The same matching logic extends past this list too; families in other countries and time zones use an identical process, just against their own school calendar. Where a family does want in-person contact, for younger students, or simply because the household prefers it, home tutoring is checked against tutor availability in that specific city, and it is fair to say some cities have a thinner pool of AI HL specialists willing to travel than others; Delhi, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar and Ghaziabad families should expect that home options vary more than online ones do. The practical takeaway: state a location honestly when booking, because it changes what's realistically offered, not just what's convenient to promise.

contentBlocks.heading: How AI HL Sits Inside the Wider Diploma
contentBlocks.body: Math AI HL is one subject inside six that make up the full IB Diploma Programme, and the tutoring plan around it usually has to account for what else is competing for the student's time: the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, CAS hours and five other subjects at SL or HL. A tutor who only thinks about AI HL in isolation can end up setting homework that is technically reasonable but lands the week the EE draft is due, which is why a first conversation should cover the whole term's competing deadlines, not just the Math ones. For students who took Math AI at SL and are considering the jump to HL, or the reverse, the honest advice is that Grade 10 into Grade 11 is a far easier point to move than after Grade 11 mocks; a late switch narrows what's achievable and should be discussed openly rather than assumed away. Students working across the Middle Years Programme into the Diploma benefit from an early look at what AI HL actually rewards, since MYP mathematics assessment criteria and DP criterion-related marking share a family resemblance but are not identical, and a tutor who has taught both stages can flag that gap before it becomes a Grade 11 surprise rather than after. Coverage spans Grade 6 through Grade 12, so pre-Diploma groundwork and full HL exam preparation sit on the same platform rather than being treated as separate services.
items: EE, TOK and CAS compete for the same weeks as Math homework
SL-to-HL switches are easiest before Grade 11 mocks
MYP-to-DP transition benefits from early exposure to DP criteria
Coverage spans Grade 6 through Grade 12 on one platform

contentBlocks.heading: What Happens Between Booking and the First Session
contentBlocks.body: A family submits the subject, the grade, the current school and the nearest deadline, whether a mock, an IA draft or a final exam, and matching starts from that, not from a generic tutor list. A tutor's own exam-board familiarity and recent AI HL teaching experience are checked against that specific request, because a tutor who has taught AI SL extensively but not the HL-only content is a weaker match even with a strong general Math background. Scheduling is worked out around the family's time zone if the session is online, or a tutor's travel range if it is home-based, before a first session is confirmed, not after, which avoids the common frustration of agreeing to a tutor only to discover scheduling doesn't actually work. The first session itself has a specific job: establish where the student actually is against the school's syllabus pace, identify one or two command-term or topic gaps worth prioritising, and agree what a realistic four-week goal looks like rather than a vague 'improve at Math' target. That goal is revisited at the four-week mark deliberately, because IB terms move fast and a plan that made sense in week one can be outdated by week four if a mock has landed or an IA deadline moved. If the fit isn't right after that first session, a personality mismatch, or a tutor whose actual specialism turns out narrower than expected, a family can ask for a different match, and that request is treated as normal, not as a complaint.

AI HL-specific experience checked, not just general Math background
Scheduling confirmed before the tutor, not after

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Tutor Is Suggested to You
contentBlocks.body: IB Gram checks a tutor's qualifications, subject background and IB or exam-board teaching experience before that tutor is offered as a match. The criteria are specific: has this person taught AI HL recently, do they understand GDC-based exam technique, have they supervised an exploration through to submission. None of this is presented as a guarantee of a particular grade, because no honest tutoring platform can promise that; a strong final result depends on far more than tutoring hours, including the student's own baseline, how much class time supports the same content, and how early tutoring started relative to the exam session. What can be promised is a process: a tutor matched on real criteria rather than availability alone, a first session that produces an actual diagnostic rather than a sales pitch, and a checked-in review point rather than an open-ended arrangement nobody revisits. Parents sometimes ask whether a cheaper, unvetted tutor found through a local classified ad does the same job for less money; sometimes it does, particularly for younger students needing general encouragement rather than HL-specific technique, and it would be dishonest to claim otherwise. Where the vetting earns its cost is at the sharp end: a student two months from a May session who has a specific IA criterion stuck, or a specific command-term pattern costing marks paper after paper, benefits from a tutor who has actually solved that exact problem before, not one encountering it for the first time alongside the student.

No promised grades — no honest platform can offer that
First session functions as a diagnostic, not a pitch
Review points built in, not an open-ended arrangement
Vetting matters most for specific, sharp-end problems

contentBlocks.heading: IB World Schools, and Where IB Gram Sits Relative to Them
contentBlocks.body: IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with the IB Organization, Cambridge International or Pearson Edexcel; a tutor sourced through the platform supplements a school's own teaching rather than replacing or representing it. That distinction matters practically, not just legally: a tutor can only see the syllabus pace and internal assessment criteria a family shares with them, so a parent who brings the actual school timeline, the specific IA rubric version and recent mock feedback gets far more useful sessions than one who describes the course in general terms. Every IB World School sets its own internal calendar within the IB's fixed May and November examination windows; mock dates, IA submission dates and even how much class time is spent on GDC technique vary school to school, which is exactly why a tutor working from a generic AI HL curriculum outline, rather than the family's actual school pace, ends up teaching the wrong week's content. Families sometimes assume a tutor needs to have taught at their exact school to be useful; that's rarely true for Math AI HL specifically, because the syllabus content is set externally by the IB Organization rather than by the school, but the internal assessment structure and pacing absolutely benefit from a tutor who asks for and works from real school documents rather than assuming a standard timeline.

Bring the actual school syllabus pace and IA rubric to sessions
Mock and IA dates are set per-school inside fixed IB windows
Content is IB-set; pacing is school-set — tutors need both

contentBlocks.heading: What a Parent Should See by Week Four
contentBlocks.body: By the end of four weeks of regular sessions, there are specific, checkable things a parent should be able to point to, not a vague sense that things are 'going well.' The student should be able to name the one or two topics or command terms the tutor identified as priorities in the first session, and say whether they've actually improved on those in recent class or mock work. There should be a visible pattern in past-paper practice: which paper, which topics, and roughly what mark-scheme technique was corrected, rather than a pile of completed worksheets with no record of what changed. If the student is mid-exploration, week four is a reasonable point to have a first full draft reviewed against specific criteria, not just a general 'looks fine' comment. If none of that exists after four weeks, no named priorities, no visible pattern, no specific IA feedback, that's the honest signal to raise it directly with the tutor or ask IB Gram for a different match, not to wait another month hoping it self-corrects. This is also the point where a family should say plainly if a mock result didn't move, because a tutor adjusting an approach in week five is far more useful than one who only finds out at the next parent call two months later.
items: Named priority topics from session one, checked against real progress
A visible pattern across past-paper work, not just volume
IA draft reviewed against specific criteria by week four
No visible pattern by week four is a signal to act, not wait

contentBlocks.heading: Getting a Tutor in Place Before the Next Deadline
contentBlocks.body: Most families reach this page already knowing what's due, a mock, an IA draft, a resit, and the useful next step is simply stating that clearly rather than searching for one more comparison article. Booking starts with the basics: current grade, the school's own timeline if it's known, and whether online, home or hybrid fits the household better. A home request is checked against real tutor availability in that city rather than promised on the spot, and online requests are matched against the family's own time zone immediately. A short first session establishes where the student actually stands against the syllabus and sets one specific four-week goal, which is a far more useful outcome than a general 'let's see how it goes' arrangement. Families rebuilding after a disappointing mock, or starting HL prep from a standing start close to a session date, should say so plainly when booking; the plan built for a student six months out looks nothing like the plan built for one eight weeks out, and pretending otherwise wastes the sessions that are actually left. For a family still deciding between AA and AI, or SL and HL, that question is worth raising before booking rather than after, since it changes which tutor is actually the right match from the first session onward.
items: State the actual deadline: mock, IA draft or resit
Say if it's a late start — the plan changes accordingly
Home requests checked against real city availability
One specific four-week goal set in the first session
Raise AA vs AI or SL vs HL doubts before booking, not after

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work for a subject as technical as AI HL?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one condition: the tutor needs to screen-share the graphic display calculator and any spreadsheet work, not just talk through it, because AI HL leans on that technology throughout its exam papers. Where online genuinely struggles is with younger students who lose focus on video calls, or households without a stable connection during the family's evening hours. For a Grade 10 to Grade 12 student preparing past papers and IA technique, online sessions with proper screen sharing generally match or beat in-person sessions, mainly because the specialist pool available online is far larger than whoever happens to be reachable locally.

faqs.question: What do the fees actually depend on?
faqs.answer: Fees are not fixed platform-wide. They depend on the tutor's experience level, whether sessions are online, home or hybrid, the frequency booked each week, and sometimes the urgency of the request, such as booking two weeks before a mock. IB Gram doesn't publish a single rate card because a newly qualified AI HL specialist and a tutor with a decade of HL exam-board experience are genuinely different services. The honest approach is to ask for a quote against your specific situation, grade, deadline and mode, rather than comparing a generic advertised number across different tutors and services.

faqs.question: What if my child makes no progress after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: Raise it directly and early rather than waiting for a term to finish. The four-week check-in exists specifically to catch this: if there's no named priority topic, no visible change in past-paper marks, and no specific IA feedback by then, that's grounds to ask for a different tutor match, not a reason to feel you made a bad decision. Sometimes the issue is genuinely a mismatch in teaching style rather than tutor quality, and switching resolves it within a session or two. IB Gram treats a tutor-swap request as routine, not as a complaint that needs justifying.

faqs.question: Can we change tutors if it isn't working out?
faqs.answer: Yes. A mismatch is common enough that it's built into how matching works rather than treated as an exception; personality fit matters as much as subject expertise for a subject students often already feel anxious about. If a first session or two makes clear the tutor's actual AI HL experience is thinner than expected, or the teaching pace doesn't suit the student, ask for a different match. There's no fixed penalty for doing this, though it does mean losing the continuity of whatever the first tutor had already learned about the student's specific gaps.

faqs.question: My child is strong at Math generally but weak specifically on the IA — does a tutor help with that?
faqs.answer: Yes, though the help has a boundary worth understanding upfront: a tutor can guide the choice of topic, question the mathematical reasoning, and check technique and communication against the assessment criteria, but the mathematical exploration itself has to be the student's own work under IB academic honesty rules. Where tutoring makes the biggest difference is in the criteria that are learnable independent of raw ability, communication, use of technology, reflection, which a student can often lift noticeably in a few focused sessions even when the underlying mathematics idea is already sound.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who taught AA HL well also good for AI HL?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, and it's worth asking directly rather than assuming. AI HL rewards modelling, statistics, financial mathematics and calculator-based technique more heavily than AA HL, which leans toward pure technique and proof; a tutor strong in one doesn't necessarily transfer cleanly to the other. contentBlocks.heading: What a Tutor Does That a Classroom Cannot
contentBlocks.body:
A school teacher for IB Mathematics is responsible for the whole class: covering the syllabus on schedule, setting the same homework for thirty students at different levels, and moving on once the term plan says to move on. That is the job, and it is not a criticism of the teacher — no classroom can pause for one student's confusion over related rates or vectors without leaving the rest of the room behind. IB Mathematics tutors do the opposite job. They start from where your child actually is, not where the syllabus says they should be, whether that is Grade 6 arithmetic fluency or a Grade 12 student two months from the May session with a Paper 2 weakness.

IB Gram works with families whose children sit anywhere from Grade 6 to Grade 12, across both the Analysis and Approaches and the Applications and Interpretation courses, at Standard and Higher Level. Because IB assessment is criterion-related rather than a simple mark tally, and because IB Mathematics rewards precise use of command terms — show, justify, hence, deduce — a tutor's job includes teaching the student how the paper is actually marked, not only the mathematics itself. Academic honesty rules apply to coursework the same way they do at school, and a tutor who does not understand that boundary is not doing the family a favour. This distinction, more than any slogan, is why parents look for a tutor once the school year is already under way.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Pairs a Family With a Tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Matching starts with specifics, not a general request for 'a maths tutor'. IB Gram asks which course the student is on — Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation — and at which level, Standard or Higher, because a tutor strong in one is not automatically the right fit for the other. Grade, target exam session (May or November), and the areas already flagged by the school's own reports narrow the shortlist further. Time zone matters as much as subject knowledge: a family in one country and a tutor in another can still work well together, but only if session times are agreed before the first class, not after.

Once a shortlist exists, the family sees tutor background and subject specialism before committing to anything. A first session is treated as a diagnostic, not a sales pitch: the tutor works through a recent test or a past-paper question with the student and forms a view on where the real gap sits, which is often different from what the parent assumed it was. That view is shared back in plain terms. If the fit is wrong — pace, teaching style, or simply personality — IB Gram arranges a different tutor rather than asking the family to persevere through discomfort. Ongoing sessions are then set against a simple cadence: a weekly goal, a running note of what was covered, and a check-in roughly every four weeks to see whether the plan needs adjusting before the next assessment deadline arrives.

Target exam session and time zone matched before scheduling

contentBlocks.heading: Where Students Usually Ask for Help First
contentBlocks.body:
Ask ten IB Mathematics tutors which topics generate the most tutoring requests and the answers cluster fast: functions and transformations in the early years, then calculus once differentiation and integration arrive, then probability and statistics for students who find the abstraction of pure algebra harder than a concrete data set. Vectors and complex numbers tend to surface for Higher Level students closer to the exam, partly because they appear late in most school schemes of work and there is less revision time left once they are taught.

The internal assessment is its own category of difficulty, separate from exam content. Choosing a topic that is mathematically rich enough to explore but narrow enough to finish, structuring the exploration so it reads as genuine inquiry rather than a solved textbook exercise, and using notation consistently — these are coaching problems, not knowledge gaps, and a tutor who has read enough IAs recognises the pattern quickly. Past-paper practice matters just as much, but only when it goes beyond 'more questions': working through mark schemes line by line, understanding why a method mark was or was not awarded, and building the exam-technique habits that a rushed student drops under time pressure. Mock results, when shared with the tutor, usually save several sessions of guessing where to start.

contentBlocks.heading: Fitting Around the IB Diploma Timeline
contentBlocks.body:
IB Mathematics tutoring sits inside a two-year Diploma Programme timeline that each school controls, not IB Gram. Internal assessment deadlines, mock exam dates and the choice between the May and November examination sessions are set by the school, and a tutor's plan has to work backward from those dates rather than around them. A student sitting the May session needs a different rhythm in October than one sitting in November, and a tutor who ignores that is planning for an exam that is not actually the one coming up.

For younger students, Middle Years Programme mathematics in Grade 6 to Grade 10 lays the groundwork that Diploma Mathematics assumes is solid: algebraic manipulation, coordinate geometry, basic statistics. A student who reaches Grade 11 with gaps in that foundation will struggle with Diploma content regardless of how good the DP-level teaching is, which is why some families start tutoring earlier than the exam years, specifically to close MYP-level gaps before they compound. IB Gram does not set curriculum policy and works entirely within whatever pace and content each school has already committed to; the tutor's task is to reinforce and clarify a school's own teaching, not to replace or contradict it. Concept-based learning, a hallmark of the IB approach, means a tutor who only drills procedure without addressing the underlying concept is not actually doing IB Mathematics tutoring at all.
items: Plans built backward from May or November exam dates
MYP-to-DP transition gaps addressed before Grade 11
IA and mock deadlines set by the school, not IB Gram
Concept-based teaching, not procedure drilling alone

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tutoring Depends on Where the Tutor Already Travels
contentBlocks.body:
Online tutoring removes geography from the equation entirely: a specialist AA Higher Level tutor working from one city can teach a student in another country in the family's own evening, with nothing lost except the option of an in-person whiteboard. That is the default IB Gram works from, because it is the only mode that guarantees subject-level fit over location.

Home tutoring is different, and worth being honest about. It depends entirely on whether a tutor already lives near enough to travel without the commute eating into the session itself. Families in cities such as Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Chandigarh, Chennai, Coimbatore, Dehradun, Delhi, Faridabad, Ghaziabad and Greater Noida ask about home tutoring often enough that it is worth naming plainly: availability varies street by street within these cities, not just city by city, and a tutor who can reach one part of a city comfortably may not be able to reach another without losing an hour each way to traffic. Where home tutoring is not realistic — a tutor two hours away, or simply none nearby who teaches AA at the required level — a hybrid arrangement usually works better than forcing an in-person model that will not survive a wet Tuesday commute. Ask about home availability specifically for your area rather than assuming a city name alone settles it.

Home tutoring depends on tutor proximity, not just city
Cities such as Delhi, Bangalore, Chennai and Chandigarh see frequent home-tutor enquiries
Hybrid plans where daily home travel is not realistic

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing Between Online, Home and Hybrid
contentBlocks.body:
Online tutoring gives access to a specialist tutor regardless of which city, or which country, the family happens to be in. For a subject like IB Mathematics, where AA Higher Level and AI Standard Level genuinely need different teaching approaches, that access matters more than proximity does. A shared digital whiteboard, screen-shared past papers and a stable video call cover most of what an in-person session offers, with the exception of a tutor physically pointing at a student's handwriting mid-calculation — a small loss for most students, a real one for a few who need that immediacy.

Home tutoring suits younger learners best, particularly in the Grade 6 to Grade 8 range, where sitting beside a tutor at the family table helps concentration in a way a screen sometimes does not. It also suits families who are simply better served by a fixed weekly rhythm in the same room. The trade-off is availability: a home tutor has to already be teaching in, or near, the family's area, which narrows the field compared with online.

Hybrid plans are the honest middle ground for families who want both: weekly online sessions for steady coverage, with an occasional in-person session before a mock or a mark-scheme-heavy revision block, arranged when a suitable tutor's schedule and travel allow it.
items: Online: full access to subject specialists, any location
Home: works well for Grade 6-8, fixed in-room rhythm
Hybrid: weekly online plus occasional in-person sessions
Trade-off is proximity versus tutor choice

contentBlocks.heading: Working Alongside Your Child's School, Not Around It
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform. It is not affiliated with the IB Organization, with Cambridge International or with Pearson Edexcel, and it has no relationship with any individual school that determines curriculum pace, IA deadlines or mock exam dates for a Diploma cohort. That distinction matters practically, not just legally: a tutor's role is to reinforce what a school is already teaching, using the same command-term conventions and the same criterion language the school's own assessments use, rather than introducing a competing method that confuses a student under pressure.

In practice this means a tutor asks to see recent school test papers, teacher feedback and IA drafts wherever the family can share them, because that feedback usually says more about the real gap than a general diagnostic test would. A student marked down on Paper 3 investigation writing, for instance, needs different help from one losing marks on Paper 1 algebraic manipulation, and the school's own comments usually point straight at which one it is. Where a school runs its own revision sessions or IA supervision, tutoring is planned to sit alongside that timetable rather than duplicate it — repeating content a student has already covered twice wastes a session that could have closed an actual gap instead.

Tutor works from the school's own tests and IA feedback
Same command-term and criterion language as the school

contentBlocks.heading: The Vetting Behind Every Tutor Match
contentBlocks.body:
Every tutor on IB Gram is reviewed for subject-specific background before being offered to a family, not just a general teaching qualification. For IB Mathematics that means confirming which course the tutor actually teaches — Analysis and Approaches, Applications and Interpretation, or both — at which level, and how recently they have worked with live IB cohorts rather than a different board's syllabus that happens to look similar on paper. Subject depth is checked separately from communication style, because a tutor who understands the mathematics perfectly can still be a poor fit for a student who needs more patience than pace.

Academic background is verified: degree subject, any teaching experience, and where relevant, examining or marking experience with an IB-recognised syllabus. None of this is announced to families as a marketing claim; it is simply the baseline before a tutor's profile is shown at all. Parents are encouraged to ask direct questions in the first session — which topics the tutor teaches most often, how they usually structure an hour, what they would flag after seeing the student's last test — and to treat vague answers as useful information in themselves. A tutor who cannot describe their own method plainly is unlikely to explain a mark scheme plainly either.

Recent experience with live IB cohorts verified
Academic background and any examining experience checked
