Physics, Chemistry — common with AA HL for STEM-leaning students
Economics, Biology — for applied or life-science routes
English A — writing quality affects grades across subjects
Cross-subject pacing (e.g. Physics and Math AA HL) coordinated where useful

contentBlocks.heading: The School Clusters This Page Is Written For
contentBlocks.body: Dehradun's IB-oriented families tend to cluster around a few identifiable school routes rather than being spread evenly across the city, and it helps to name them plainly. There's the Rajpur Road corridor, running through Jakhan and up toward Mussoorie Road, which carries a mix of day and boarding families used to premium schooling. Central Dehradun — Dalanwala, EC Road and the Race Course area — has its own cluster, generally easier for home-tutor travel because the roads are more predictable and central. West Dehradun, covering Vasant Vihar and Prem Nagar, is a third distinct pocket, often a longer drive from the Rajpur Road side, which is exactly why online or hybrid support gets suggested more often for families here when a strong subject match happens to live elsewhere in the city. None of this means IB Gram is attached to any particular school — it is an independent tutoring platform, not affiliated with any school named or implied here unless specifically stated, and it works from what a family tells it about their child's actual school situation rather than assuming a curriculum pace from the postcode alone. Two students at the same school, even in the same grade, can be at very different points with Math AA HL — one comfortable with proof, another still shaky on algebraic manipulation — so the school cluster explains logistics and context, not what to teach in the first session.

contentBlocks.heading: Being Straightforward About What Improvement Looks Like
contentBlocks.body: No tutor can promise a particular grade, and any promise of a guaranteed 7 or a fixed score jump should be treated as a warning sign rather than reassurance — IB assessment simply doesn't work that way, and a family that hears an unconditional guarantee is right to ask harder questions. What IB Gram can describe honestly is the process: subject background is checked, exam-board familiarity with the current AA HL syllabus is discussed, and fit is reviewed against the student's actual starting point rather than an assumed one. Progress is meant to be visible, not asserted — a parent should be able to see, around four weeks in, whether the student is attempting harder problem types unprompted, whether timed practice scores are trending in a direction, and whether the student can explain a solution method rather than just reproduce it. If none of that is happening by week four, that is itself useful information, and it is a normal point to review whether the tutor, the pace, or the format needs to change, rather than waiting out a full term hoping it self-corrects. Concept-based learning matters here too: academic honesty rules mean a tutor helping with an IA or an assignment is expected to develop the student's thinking, not produce work for them, and a Dehradun family should expect that boundary to be respected even under exam-season pressure, when the temptation to just hand over an answer is highest.

Subject background and syllabus familiarity checked before matching
Week-four check: harder problems attempted, scores trending, methods explained

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Tutor Is Suggested
contentBlocks.body: Before a Math AA HL tutor is suggested for a Dehradun family, a few concrete things are looked at rather than taken on trust: the tutor's own subject background at the level being taught, prior experience with the Analysis and Approaches syllabus specifically rather than a generic Class 12 maths background, and comfort with the assessment structure — Paper 1 without a calculator, Paper 2 and 3 with one, and how the internal assessment fits into that. Familiarity with command-term language matters more than it sounds; a tutor who can explain the difference between 'show that' and 'hence show that' in a mark-scheme sense is doing something a generic tutor usually can't. Availability and realistic scheduling are checked too, because a tutor who says yes to a slot they can't actually sustain across a term does a family no favours. None of this is described as a fixed checklist applied identically every time — depth of vetting can vary by subject rarity and by how urgent the request is, and it is always subject to tutor availability at the time of the request. What's promised instead is transparency: a family can ask what was checked for their specific match, and get a real answer rather than a marketing line. For a specialist subject like Math AA HL, where a shallow maths background shows up quickly once past-paper technique starts, this matters more than it would for a broader subject.

AA syllabus and paper structure (P1 non-calculator, P2/P3 calculator) familiarity checked

A request that says 'need a Math AA HL tutor' gets a slower, more generic response than one that says which point in the DP year the student is at, what the last test or mock score was, whether the family is closer to Rajpur Road or Prem Nagar, and whether home, online or hybrid is preferred. That context is exactly what lets IB Gram review the request against the right kind of tutor rather than the first available one. It also helps to mention what else is on the plate — an EE in a different subject, a TOK presentation coming up, a sibling in MYP needing separate support — because scheduling around a real week is more useful than scheduling around an idealised one. For families weighing the May 2026 or November 2026 session, timing the first conversation matters: starting the request in the same month a mock is announced leaves less room to build proof fluency before technique work has to take over. Starting earlier, even a term earlier, buys room to do both properly. None of this requires committing to anything before a first session happens — it's a request for review, not a booking, and the honest answer sometimes is that a particular week or area combination needs a slightly different format than what was first asked for.

faqs.question: How much does an IB Math AA HL tutor in Dehradun cost?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the tutor's experience, whether sessions are home, online or hybrid, and how many sessions a week the family wants — there isn't one fixed number IB Gram can quote before a request is reviewed. Home tutoring in areas like Rajpur Road or Dalanwala can carry a different rate than online sessions with a specialist HL tutor based elsewhere, since travel and subject rarity both factor in. The honest approach is to share the student's level and preferred format first; a specific range comes back once a match is reviewed, rather than a generic number that doesn't reflect Math AA HL's specialist nature.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring actually effective for a subject like Math AA HL?
faqs.answer: For HL mathematics specifically, yes, more often than families expect — a shared digital whiteboard handles algebra and graphing well, and screen-sharing makes past-paper walkthroughs easier to follow than a shared notebook page. It suits boarding students and vacation revision particularly well, since it doesn't depend on a physical location. Where online is weaker is for a student who needs someone physically present to stay focused, or for very young learners who benefit from in-room presence. For a Grade 11 or 12 DP student doing focused HL practice, online is usually not a compromise — it's often the format that gets the better subject-matched tutor in the first place.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor isn't a good fit after a few sessions?
faqs.answer: It happens, and it isn't treated as an unusual complaint. Fit problems usually show up as pace mismatch, a communication style that doesn't suit the student, or a tutor stronger in theory than in past-paper technique when the student actually needed the reverse. IB Gram reviews a change request the same way it reviewed the original one — student level, format, area or online preference, and what specifically didn't work this time, so the next suggestion corrects for it rather than repeating the same mismatch. Raising this early, inside the first two or three sessions, is more useful than waiting out a full month hoping it improves on its own.

faqs.question: Can a tutor cover both Math AA HL and Physics for the same student?
faqs.answer: IB Gram can review requests for both subjects together, and it often helps when the two tutors — whether the same person or two people — coordinate pacing, since HL mechanics and fields problems depend directly on calculus and vectors from Math AA HL. A student relearning the same calculus concept twice, once loosely in physics class and once properly in maths tutoring, loses time either way. Whether one tutor genuinely covers both well depends on their own subject depth; a physics specialist isn't automatically strong at HL proof technique, so this is checked rather than assumed when a combined request comes in.

faqs.question: We live in Prem Nagar — is home tutoring realistic for us?
faqs.answer: It depends on the tutor's own base and travel route more than on Prem Nagar itself. Areas like Sudhowala and Nanda Ki Chowki sit further from the Rajpur Road and Dalanwala corridor where more tutors are typically based, so a repeatable weekly home slot can be harder to sustain than in central Dehradun. That's not a reason to rule out home tutoring outright, but it is a reason IB Gram often suggests online or hybrid for West Dehradun families needing a specialist subject like Math AA HL, so the search for subject depth isn't limited to who can comfortably reach Prem Nagar every week.

faqs.question: How is IA support different from just getting answers?
faqs.answer: IA support under IB rules means helping a student structure their approach, question their method and understand the assessment criteria — it does not mean writing or solving the assessed work itself, which would break academic honesty rules the school and IB Organization both take seriously. A tutor's role is closer to a structured second opinion: is the research question well-scoped, does the mathematical exploration go deep enough, is the write-up matching what the criteria actually reward. Families sometimes want more direct help than this allows, and it's worth saying plainly that IB Gram tutors are expected to hold this line even when a deadline is close.

faqs.question: What does a first session with a Math AA HL tutor actually cover?
faqs.answer: It's treated as a diagnostic rather than a jump into new content. A tutor typically reviews recent test or mock scripts, asks the student to work through a problem or two out loud to see where reasoning breaks down, and checks comfort with foundational topics like functions and algebra that later HL content assumes. From there, a short plan for the first month is set, with specific weekly goals a parent can see rather than a vague sense of 'covering the syllabus.' If IA work is already underway, the first session usually also covers where that stands and what needs attention next.

faqs.question: Does a boarding-school student really need a different plan than a day-school student?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, mainly around scheduling rather than content. A boarding student can't take home sessions during term, so online tutoring timed around hostel routines is usually the workable format, with more concentrated in-person catch-up possible only during vacation blocks back home. A day-school student in Dalanwala or Vasant Vihar has more scheduling flexibility week to week but may have less exposure to varied problem sets outside class hours. Both situations are common in Dehradun given its boarding-school culture, and the plan a tutor builds should reflect which one applies rather than assuming a standard weekday-evening rhythm works for everyone.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum number of sessions we need to commit to?
faqs.answer: No fixed minimum is required before a family can review whether a match is working — a first session and a short follow-up conversation are usually enough to tell if the pace and communication style suit the student. Beyond that, a term-length commitment tends to be more useful for HL mathematics specifically, since proof habits and technique build over weeks rather than in isolated sessions, but that is a scheduling conversation between the family and tutor rather than a fixed IB Gram rule. Sessions and frequency stay subject to what the family and tutor agree, and can be revisited as the exam session approaches.

faqs.question: What if my child is starting Math AA HL late, partway through Grade 12?
faqs.answer: It's harder, and it's worth being honest about that rather than promising an easy catch-up. Starting HL-level work with only months before a May or November session limits how much foundational rebuilding is realistic, so the priority usually shifts toward the highest-yield topics and past-paper technique rather than a full ground-up rebuild of every unit. A switch from AI to AA this late is rarely advisable for the same reason. IB Gram tutors reviewing a late-start request are expected to say plainly what's achievable in the time available, rather than agreeing to a plan that quietly assumes more time than actually exists.

contentBlocks.heading: Judging an Hour of Tutoring by What It Produces
contentBlocks.body: Dehradun's IB market is unusual for a tier-two city. International schools built around boarding culture and premium day admissions have created real demand for tutors who understand Diploma Programme mechanics, not generic board coaching, and parents here compare rates before committing to a term. That comparison should not stop at the number. An hour of IB Math AI HL tutoring is worth judging by what a student can do afterward that they could not do before it: read a command term accurately, work a GDC-based Paper 2 question through to a sensible answer, or explain why a statistical model suited an IA rather than running the numbers. Math Applications and Interpretation rewards students who connect real-world context to technique, and a tutor who only drills algebra without that context is charging for the wrong hour. Some families here are local; others are outstation or overseas parents tracking a boarding-school student remotely, and for them the hour's value includes visibility — a note on what was covered, a read on whether pace matches ahead of the May 2026 or November 2026 exam session. IB Gram treats that visibility as part of the hour, not an extra. Honest caveat: a single session cannot fix months of gaps, and a tutor who claims otherwise early is worth doubting.

Command-term accuracy: 'justify' vs 'suggest' vs 'determine'

Weekly note on topics covered and pace toward the exam session

contentBlocks.heading: Where Math AI HL Sits Among Dehradun's DP Subjects
contentBlocks.body: Math AI HL is one of two Diploma Programme maths routes, and Dehradun families often reach out only after realising the difference matters. Math Applications and Interpretation is built around modelling, technology and statistics — GDC use is assumed, not optional, and problems sit inside a real context: population growth, correlation, network problems, kinematics, unlike AA's proof-heavy style. Math AA HL leans toward algebraic manipulation and formal proof; a student who finds proof slow but reads a word problem comfortably usually does better on the AI route. A tutor who has taught both routes tends to explain this distinction more honestly than one who has only taught AA. Beyond maths, Dehradun's DP cohort commonly pairs Math AI HL with Physics, Chemistry, Economics, Biology or English A, and the combination affects scheduling: a student doing Physics HL alongside Math AI HL needs a tutor comfortable with calculus-adjacent physics, while an Economics pairing leans on statistics and correlation work. IB Gram checks which subjects a tutor can teach at HL versus SL before suggesting a match, rather than assuming a maths tutor covers every science by default. Families juggling several DP subjects sometimes want one tutor for two of them, which is possible but should be confirmed subject by subject, not assumed from a general profile.
items: Math AI HL: modelling, statistics, GDC-based problem solving
Math AA HL: algebraic proof and formal reasoning

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: Same Platform, Different Kind of Help
contentBlocks.body: IB Gram works across the full run of IB programmes taught in Dehradun: the Primary Years Programme for ages 3 to 12, the Middle Years Programme for ages 11 to 16, and the Diploma Programme for ages 16 to 19, covering Grade 1 to Grade 12 overall. What counts as good tutoring looks different at each stage. A PYP student generally needs gentle support with reading, numeracy and unit-of-inquiry work — the goal is confidence and curiosity, not content coverage, and a tutor who treats a seven-year-old like a mini DP student is doing it wrong. An MYP student is usually further along technically but still learning to turn a broad classroom prompt into criterion-ready work: understanding what a rubric is actually asking for is often the missing skill, more than subject knowledge itself. A DP student doing Math AI HL needs something else again — a subject specialist who can handle HL depth, plan an IA around a genuine mathematical exploration, prepare for Paper 1, 2 and 3 timing, and stay alert to the TOK connections examiners increasingly expect referenced across subjects, all without quietly taking over work meant to be the student's own. IB Gram matches on this basis rather than assuming one tutor profile suits every age; a specialist strong with DP HL is not automatically the right fit for a Grade 3 inquiry project, and IB Gram checks that before suggesting a match.

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Tutor Is Suggested
contentBlocks.body: Before a tutor's name reaches a Dehradun family, IB Gram checks a specific set of things, and it is worth saying plainly what is and is not verified. Subject background is checked against what is actually being taught — a tutor claiming Math AI HL should be able to speak fluently about GDC-based technique, statistical modelling and the difference between AI and AA, not just general '12th maths.' Familiarity with IB's own assessment language is checked too: command terms, criterion-related marking, concept-based learning rather than rote formula recall, and the distinction between formative feedback and doing assessed work for a student. A tutor who cannot explain what academic honesty means in an IA context is not a fit for DP-level work, however strong their general subject knowledge. Experience with the specific pressure points of a DP year — internal assessments, mock exam cycles, reviewing school-set assignments before they are submitted, and the run-up to the May 2026 or November 2026 session — is weighed alongside raw subject knowledge, because a tutor who is excellent at content but has never sat with a student through IA panic is missing something families notice quickly. What IB Gram does not do is promise a fixed number of years of experience or a guaranteed outcome; verification is about fit and competence, not a marketing badge. Parents are encouraged to use the first session as their own check: ask the tutor to walk through a past-paper question live, notice whether they explain the reasoning or just the answer, and see whether they ask the student clarifying questions rather than talking at them for forty-five minutes straight.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Hybrid: Picking the Right Shape
contentBlocks.body: Three formats are on the table for Dehradun families, and each suits a different situation rather than one being universally better. Home tutoring can be reviewed in the central residential pockets already covered — Rajpur Road, Dalanwala, Mussoorie Road, Vasant Vihar and Prem Nagar — and works well for younger learners who benefit from someone physically present, and for families whose home sits close to a tutor's existing travel route. It is generally weaker for very specialised DP subjects, where the right specialist may simply not live in Dehradun at all, and for households where evening traffic makes a reliable time slot hard to hold. Online tutoring is available city-wide and tends to be the stronger option for exactly those situations: boarding students who are only home for part of the year, HL subjects where specialist supply is thin locally, urgent doubt-clearing before a test, and the intense revision windows before the May 2026 or November 2026 exam sessions when a student may need a session on short notice regardless of where the tutor happens to live. Hybrid plans combine both — a home tutor for weekly accountability and structure, plus online sessions with a specialist for IA guidance or a particular HL topic — and this often ends up being the practical answer for a Math AI HL student who wants consistent in-person habit-building but also needs someone who has actually taught the AI syllabus at HL. None of the three is automatically right; the honest starting point is the student's actual weekly schedule and where the family is willing to compromise.

Progress in Math AI HL specifically tends to show up as fewer mechanical errors on GDC-based questions, a student who can explain why a technique applies to a given context instead of just applying it by memory, and steadier scores across successive practice papers rather than one lucky mark. None of this is instant; a student starting IA planning eight weeks before the deadline has real constraints a tutor cannot simply tutor their way around, and it is more honest to say so than to promise otherwise.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IB Math AI HL and Math AA HL?
faqs.answer: Math AI HL — Applications and Interpretation — is built around modelling, statistics, technology and GDC use, with problems set in real-world contexts like population growth or correlation. Math AA HL — Analysis and Approaches — leans toward algebraic manipulation, formal proof and calculus worked by hand. A student who finds proof-based reasoning slow but reads word problems comfortably usually does better on AI. The two are genuinely different syllabuses, not the same content at different difficulty, so a tutor who has only taught AA may not automatically translate to AI, and it is worth confirming that background directly.

faqs.question: How much does an IB Math AI HL tutor in Dehradun cost?
faqs.answer: Fees vary by tutor experience, session format and how much HL-specific and IA-support work is needed, so IB Gram does not quote a single fixed number upfront. What matters more than the headline rate is what an hour includes — genuine command-term explanation, GDC technique, and IA guidance, versus generic problem-walkthroughs a student could get from a recorded video. A fair way to judge value is to ask what will be different after four sessions, not just what the hourly rate is. Home and online sessions are priced differently, and rates should be confirmed directly during matching.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring actually effective for IB Math AI HL, or is home tutoring always better?
faqs.answer: Online tutoring works well for Math AI HL specifically because so much of the subject runs through a GDC and a shared digital workspace anyway — screen-sharing a graph or a spreadsheet model translates naturally online. It tends to be the stronger option for boarding students, for HL specialist access when the right tutor is not physically nearby, and during the intense revision stretch before the May 2026 or November 2026 exams. Home tutoring has its own advantage for younger or less self-directed students who focus better with someone physically present. There is no blanket rule here; the right call depends on the student's habits and the specific gap being addressed.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Prem Nagar or Vasant Vihar for home sessions, given how far west they are?
faqs.answer: Home tutoring can be reviewed for Vasant Vihar and Prem Nagar, but travel realism depends on which tutor is being matched and their existing schedule — a tutor already covering Ballupur or Sudhowala is a more natural fit than one based near Rajpur Road trying to add a western pocket to the same evening. Dehradun's traffic around school-closing hours makes cross-town travel slower than distance alone suggests, so a request from this side of the city is checked against realistic timing rather than assumed possible by default. Where a good travel-matched home tutor is not readily available, online tutoring or a hybrid plan is usually the more reliable option for consistent scheduling.

faqs.question: What if my child is starting IB Math AI HL preparation late, close to the exam?
faqs.answer: Starting late narrows what is realistically achievable, and an honest tutor will say so rather than promising full coverage in a few weeks. Late-stage support usually focuses on the highest-yield topics — the ones that appear most reliably across Paper 1 and Paper 2 — past-paper technique under timed conditions, and closing specific gaps the student's own mock results point to, rather than re-teaching the syllabus from the beginning. If an IA is still outstanding, that becomes the priority alongside exam content, since it carries independent marks and has its own deadline pressure. Families should expect a tutor to say plainly what is and is not possible in the remaining time, rather than reassuring vaguely.

faqs.question: How does IB Gram handle IA and EE support without crossing into doing the work for the student?
faqs.answer: A tutor's role in IA and EE support is to question, structure and check — helping a student pick a workable topic, sharpen a research question, or spot where a method does not match the data — not to write sentences that end up in the submitted document. IB's academic honesty rules exist precisely to protect authentic student work, and IB Gram expects tutors to work within them. In practice this looks like a tutor asking 'why did you choose this approach' more often than supplying the answer, and reviewing a draft for gaps in reasoning rather than rewriting it. A family that wants the second kind of help will be told directly that it is not something IB Gram supports.

faqs.question: My child's school is a boarding school — how does scheduling work?
faqs.answer: Boarding-school students are one of the more common reasons families in Dehradun turn to online tutoring, since prep-time rules, dorm schedules and limited free evenings make regular home sessions difficult to hold. Online sessions can usually be scheduled around whatever windows the school calendar actually allows, including weekend slots or short pre-exam bursts rather than a fixed weekly slot. Parents who are themselves outstation or overseas often value the visibility that comes with online sessions — a shared note or update after each one — since they cannot always check in physically. Where a boarding student is home for a school holiday, a short run of home sessions can sometimes be reviewed alongside the usual online schedule.

faqs.question: What happens if there is no real progress after starting with a tutor?
faqs.answer: If four to six weeks pass without visible movement — no change in practice-paper scores, no clearer command-term understanding, no progress on an IA — that is a signal to raise directly rather than waiting it out. IB Gram treats a stalled match as something to review: sometimes the fix is a pacing change with the same tutor, sometimes it genuinely is a different tutor, and sometimes the honest answer is that the student needs more session frequency than the family originally budgeted for. What should not happen is a tutor insisting everything is fine while a parent's own read of test scores says otherwise; that mismatch is worth raising early rather than late.

faqs.question: Do you offer a trial session before committing to a term?
faqs.answer: Availability for a trial or first paid session depends on the specific tutor and their current schedule, so it is worth asking directly during matching rather than assuming a fixed policy. What a first session should show, regardless of terms, is whether the tutor's explanation style suits the student, whether they can speak specifically to Math AI HL content rather than general DP maths, and whether the proposed weekly structure is realistic against school timings. Families are encouraged to treat that first session as the actual decision point rather than committing to a full term on the strength of a phone call alone.

contentBlocks.heading: What Actually Drives the IB Physics Timetable in Dehradun
contentBlocks.body: An IB Physics grade is built from more pieces than a typical Class 10 or Class 12 board result, and that shapes how tutoring should be scheduled. There is the Internal Assessment, a single investigation the student designs, runs and writes up under IB's academic honesty rules, worth a fixed share of the final grade regardless of HL or SL level. There are Paper 1 and Paper 2, which test data-based and extended-response questions against precise command terms like 'evaluate', 'derive' and 'discuss'. HL students also sit Paper 3, which draws on the additional HL-only topics: further mechanics, engineering physics or astrophysics options, depending on what the school teaches. For the May 2026 and November 2026 DP sessions, this means a family cannot simply add revision hours in the last month and expect the IA mark to move; that piece is usually locked earlier in Year 1 or early Year 2. What a Dehradun family searching for support usually needs, instead, is a tutor who can map backward from these assessment components to a weekly plan: IA structure and data analysis first, then command-term practice threaded through the term, then timed paper work closer to mocks. Concept-based teaching matters here too. IB Physics rewards a student who can explain why a result holds, not just state it, so a tutor who only drills formulae is solving the wrong problem. IB Gram treats this distinction as the starting point of any match.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Matches a Family With a Physics Tutor
contentBlocks.body: A request usually starts with a short conversation about where the student is stuck: is it HL mechanics and fields, SL waves and electricity, an IA topic that hasn't been approved yet, or general confidence heading into mocks? IB Gram uses that detail, along with the student's grade, programme year and preferred mode, to shortlist tutors who have actually taught DP Physics at the right level rather than a generic physics background. A first session is usually diagnostic rather than instructional: the tutor works through a recent test, IA draft or homework set to see where the gaps sit between understanding a concept and applying it under exam conditions. From there, a short-term plan gets set, usually four to six weeks, with specific, parent-visible goals rather than vague promises of improvement. Around week four, most families and tutors review what changed: has the student stopped mixing up 'state' and 'explain' in written answers, are IA data tables cleaner, is timed paper work faster? If the fit is wrong, tutor changes are possible and, frankly, sometimes necessary; a tutor who is excellent at HL astrophysics but has thin experience with a nervous SL student in Grade 11 is not a good match, and IB Gram treats a swap request as normal rather than a failure. Scheduling is worked around the family's actual week, not a fixed slot list, since Dehradun's school timings and travel patterns vary sharply between areas.

contentBlocks.heading: Physics Alongside the Other DP Subjects Dehradun Students Take
contentBlocks.body: Physics rarely sits in isolation on a DP timetable. Most Dehradun students who ask about an IB Physics tutor are also carrying Math AA HL or Math AI HL, and Physics HL specifically leans on the calculus, vectors and logarithms that Math AA HL covers; a student weak in that math will feel it first in Physics problem sets, not in the math class itself. Group 4 combinations matter too. A student pairing Physics with Chemistry needs consistent unit conventions and significant-figure habits across both, since examiners in both subjects mark on the same underlying skills. Others pair Physics with Biology for a bioscience direction, or carry Economics alongside a full science load, which changes how much weekly time Physics can realistically claim. English A tutoring, when it is needed, is usually separate from Physics but shares the same exam-season calendar, so a family juggling both should plan revision blocks that do not collide in the weeks before May or November. IB Gram can review a family's full subject list rather than treating a Physics request as standalone, since a tutor who understands how Physics interacts with a student's Math level, or how much room is left after other subjects, plans a more realistic weekly schedule than one working from Physics content alone. This cross-subject view matters most for HL-heavy combinations, where three HL subjects leave little slack for a student who is behind in more than one of them at once.

contentBlocks.heading: Where Physics Support Fits Across PYP, MYP and the Diploma
contentBlocks.body: IB Physics as an examined subject exists inside the Diploma Programme, for students roughly aged 16 to 19, but the habits that make DP Physics workable start much earlier. In the Primary Years Programme, students aged 3 to 12 encounter physical concepts through units of inquiry rather than formal physics; a Grade 4 or 5 student struggling with a science unit needs a tutor comfortable with inquiry-based questioning, not someone reaching for DP-level formulae. The Middle Years Programme, spanning ages 11 to 16, is where formal physics content starts to resemble what DP will later demand: criterion-based assessment, structured investigations and early exposure to the kind of data analysis an IA will eventually require. A Grade 9 or 10 MYP student who struggles with graphing, uncertainty or writing a clear conclusion is often building exactly the skill an IB Physics IA will test two years later, so MYP-stage support is not throwaway groundwork. By the time a student reaches DP Physics HL or SL, the tutor's job shifts again: less about explaining a concept for the first time, more about applying it precisely under command-term instructions and paper conditions. IB Gram's grade range across Dehradun covers Grade 1 through Grade 12, so a family can look ahead: a PYP or MYP student who is already finding science difficult is a reasonable signal to address gaps before DP HL Physics arrives with far less room to recover lost ground.

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing Between Home, Online and Hybrid Physics Support
contentBlocks.body: None of the three modes is universally better, and a tutor who insists otherwise is usually protecting their own preference rather than the student's outcome. Home tutoring works well for a younger learner who needs someone physically present to keep focus, or for a family in one of the central Dehradun pockets where a tutor can realistically commit to a weekly slot without losing an hour to travel. It tends to work less well for a DP HL student who needs a specific specialist, since the pool of home tutors confident teaching HL astrophysics or engineering physics options is naturally smaller than the pool of online specialists covering the same content. Online tutoring is usually the stronger choice for boarding students who cannot host a home tutor at all, for urgent doubt-solving between sessions, for HL topics that need a specialist regardless of where they are based, and for the final stretch before May or November exams when a student needs flexible, sometimes late-evening slots that a home tutor's travel schedule cannot absorb. Hybrid plans, combining a base of in-person sessions with occasional online specialist input, suit a student who benefits from face-to-face accountability most weeks but needs, say, one HL topic covered by someone who teaches that option regularly. The honest trade-off is that hybrid needs more coordination from the family, checking that both tutors know what the other has covered, so it works best when a parent has bandwidth to manage two threads rather than one.

contentBlocks.heading: The Checks Behind Every Physics Tutor Suggestion
contentBlocks.body: A tutor being suggested for an IB Physics request in Dehradun is checked against more than general teaching experience. Subject background is reviewed first: has this person actually taught DP Physics, at HL or SL, and do they know the difference between what a Paper 2 extended-response question expects and what a school test question expects, since the two are graded on different logic. Familiarity with the current DP Physics guide matters too, because syllabus content and IA requirements have shifted across recent IB curriculum reviews, and a tutor working from an outdated guide will misjudge command-term weighting or point a student toward IA topics that no longer fit the assessment criteria cleanly. Experience with academic honesty boundaries is checked deliberately: an IA is the student's own investigation, and a tutor who edits data tables, rewrites conclusions or effectively completes sections themselves is not tutoring, it is a plagiarism risk that can cost a student their diploma. IB Gram treats this line seriously and expects tutors to explain a concept, review a draft and suggest what a stronger analysis would look like, without touching the assessed work itself. Communication style is reviewed too, since a tutor working with a Grade 11 student five months from mocks needs a different tone than one working with a Grade 6 MYP student building early lab-report habits. None of this produces a guarantee of results; it produces a tutor whose background actually matches what DP Physics specifically requires, which is the more honest thing to check for.

contentBlocks.heading: Honest Limits: What Physics Tutoring Can and Cannot Fix
contentBlocks.body: It is worth saying plainly: no tutor, however well matched, can guarantee a particular grade, and any platform claiming otherwise is not being honest with the family. What consistent IB Physics tutoring can realistically do is close specific, named gaps: a student who consistently loses marks on 'evaluate' questions because they list points instead of weighing them, a student whose IA data analysis lacks proper uncertainty propagation, a student who understands SL mechanics but freezes on HL rotational dynamics under time pressure. Progress after four weeks should look like something you can point to, not a vague feeling of improvement: fewer repeated mistakes on the same command term, a cleaner IA draft, faster and more accurate work on timed past papers. If none of that shows up after a genuine month of consistent sessions, the honest response is to review the match rather than add more hours to a plan that is not working, since more time with the wrong-fit tutor rarely fixes the underlying mismatch. There is also a real limitation worth naming: a student starting HL Physics tutoring six weeks before the May session, with major conceptual gaps across multiple topics, is not going to close all of that in six weeks, and a tutor who promises otherwise is setting the family up for disappointment. What is realistic in that situation is triage: prioritising the highest-mark-value gaps first, accepting that some weaker topics stay weaker, and being clear with the family about that trade-off from the first conversation rather than after the exam.

faqs.question: Does online IB Physics tutoring actually work, or is home tutoring always better?
faqs.answer: Online tutoring works well for IB Physics because much of what DP Physics needs, past paper questions, IA data review, talking through command terms, transfers cleanly to a shared screen. It struggles more for a young or easily distracted student who needs someone physically present to hold focus, and it depends on a quiet space and a stable connection. faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IB Physics IA topic selection specifically for a Dehradun student?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is one of the more common requests, since a poorly chosen IA topic causes more lost marks over the following months than almost anything else. A tutor reviewing IA topic ideas checks whether the investigation is genuinely researchable with the equipment and access a student realistically has, whether the variable relationships are physics-rich enough to sustain proper analysis, and whether the scope fits the time available before the school's internal deadline. For students without a home physics lab, this sometimes means steering toward topics that use accessible household or online-simulation-based setups rather than specialised apparatus. What the tutor does not do is choose the topic outright or write the analysis; IB's academic honesty rules mean the ideas and execution have to stay the student's own.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IB Physics HL and SL, and does it change what tutoring looks like?
faqs.answer: HL Physics covers everything SL does plus additional depth and extra option content, such as further mechanics, engineering physics or astrophysics depending on the school's choice, and it is examined with an extra paper, Paper 3. HL tutoring tends to spend more time on the additional option topic and on the harder end of shared topics, since HL questions probe deeper reasoning even on content SL also covers. SL tutoring can move faster through breadth but often needs more repetition on core skills like graph interpretation and unit consistency, since SL students typically have fewer weekly Physics contact hours at school. A tutor experienced only at SL may not be the right fit for an HL student tackling astrophysics, so level match matters as much as subject match.

faqs.question: How soon before the May or November exam session should we start tutoring?
faqs.answer: Earlier is better, but the honest answer depends on what is actually wrong. If the gap is exam technique, timing and command-term precision on content the student already understands, six to eight weeks of focused sessions before the exam can produce a real, visible difference. If the gap is conceptual, whole topics not properly understood, that timeline is not realistic, and starting three to four months earlier gives far more room to actually learn the material rather than cram exam tricks on top of shaky foundations. IA-related support should ideally start well before the school's own internal deadline, often a full term earlier, since a rushed IA rarely scores well regardless of how strong the student's exam technique is.

faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with the IB Organization, Cambridge, Pearson Edexcel, or any specific Dehradun school, unless a particular arrangement is stated explicitly for that case. Tutors are reviewed for their subject background, DP teaching experience and familiarity with current assessment criteria, not for a relationship with any institution. When school context is mentioned, such as which corridor a school cluster sits in, that is used only to help judge realistic travel and scheduling, not to imply endorsement by or partnership with that school. Families should treat any claim of official school or IB Organization affiliation, from any platform, with caution, since IB Diploma tutoring support is, by design, an independent, external service.

faqs.question: What does a typical first Physics session with a new tutor cover?
faqs.answer: It usually starts with a look at recent work, a test, homework set or IA draft, to see where marks are actually being lost rather than relying on the student's own sense of what is wrong. The tutor will typically ask the student to explain a concept in their own words and to attempt one or two exam-style questions live, since watching how a student approaches a command term reveals more than asking them to recite a definition. By the end of the session, most families get a short, specific plan: which topics or skills come first, roughly how many weeks a first review point should take, and what mode, home, online or hybrid, fits the weeks ahead best.

HL tutoring tends to spend more time on the additional option topic and on the harder end of shared topics, since HL questions probe deeper reasoning even on content SL also covers. SL tutoring can move faster through breadth but often needs more repetition on core skills like graph interpretation and unit consistency, since SL students typically have fewer weekly Physics contact hours at school. A tutor experienced only at SL may not be the right fit for an HL student tackling astrophysics, so level match matters as much as subject match.

mainEntity.name: How soon before the May or November exam session should we start tutoring?

acceptedAnswer.text: Earlier is better, but the honest answer depends on what is actually wrong. If the gap is exam technique, timing and command-term precision on content the student already understands, six to eight weeks of focused sessions before the exam can produce a real, visible difference. If the gap is conceptual, whole topics not properly understood, that timeline is not realistic, and starting three to four months earlier gives far more room to actually learn the material rather than cram exam tricks on top of shaky foundations. IA-related support should ideally start well before the school's own internal deadline, often a full term earlier, since a rushed IA rarely scores well regardless of how strong the student's exam technique is.

mainEntity.name: Are IB Gram tutors affiliated with specific Dehradun schools or the IB Organization?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with the IB Organization, Cambridge, Pearson Edexcel, or any specific Dehradun school, unless a particular arrangement is stated explicitly for that case. Tutors are reviewed for their subject background, DP teaching experience and familiarity with current assessment criteria, not for a relationship with any institution. When school context is mentioned, such as which corridor a school cluster sits in, that is used only to help judge realistic travel and scheduling, not to imply endorsement by or partnership with that school. Families should treat any claim of official school or IB Organization affiliation, from any platform, with caution, since IB Diploma tutoring support is, by design, an independent, external service.

mainEntity.name: What does a typical first Physics session with a new tutor cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: It usually starts with a look at recent work, a test, homework set or IA draft, to see where marks are actually being lost rather than relying on the student's own sense of what is wrong. The tutor will typically ask the student to explain a concept in their own words and to attempt one or two exam-style questions live, since watching how a student approaches a command term reveals more than asking them to recite a definition. By the end of the session, most families get a short, specific plan: which topics or skills come first, roughly how many weeks a first review point should take, and what mode, home, online or hybrid, fits the weeks ahead best.

A suitable tutor is shortlisted for home, online or hybrid sessions, subject to availability, starting with a diagnostic first session rather than a fixed sales pitch.

heroTitle: An IB Chemistry Tutor Matched to Your Timeline
heroSubtitle: This week's IA deadline, this month's mock revision, or a full term of HL support: Delhi parents come to IB Chemistry tutoring at different points of urgency, and IB Gram matches each one to a tutor who understands Paper 1, 2 and 3 demands and can actually keep a Delhi schedule.
introSummary: Looking for an IB Chemistry tutor in Delhi usually means one of three situations: a Grade 11 student confused by equilibrium and kinetics before internals, a Grade 12 student staring at an IA deadline, or a family relocating mid-year and needing someone to fill gaps fast. IB Gram works across all three. Tutors are matched by HL or SL level, by how much IA and EE support is needed, and by whether home tutoring in areas like South Delhi is realistic or online tutoring suits the family's schedule better.

contentBlocks.heading: Where Delhi Families Usually Start
contentBlocks.body:
Delhi's IB Chemistry tutoring demand rarely looks the same from one household to the next. One family is dealing with an embassy posting that ends mid-year and a Grade 11 student who has missed a full unit on organic mechanisms. Another has a Grade 12 student two months from May 2026 finals, needing focused Paper 2 and Paper 3 practice rather than a full syllabus restart. A third simply wants a steady weekly tutor from September through the November 2026 session, someone who can sit alongside the school's own pace rather than replace it.

IB Gram treats these as different requests, not the same product sold three ways. The first question a family is asked is rarely 'which tutor is best' — it is closer to 'how much time do we actually have, and what does the student need in that time.' A student three weeks from a mock needs drilling on command terms and past-paper technique. A student starting in September has room for a proper foundation in bonding, equilibrium and organic chemistry before HL problem-solving gets layered on.

Delhi adds its own layer: cross-city travel, school timings that vary by curriculum, and families who split time between South Delhi and NCR townships like Gurugram or Noida for work. A tutoring plan that ignores this ends up unrealistic within two weeks. One built around it tends to actually run for a full term.
items: This week: urgent IA or homework deadline
This month: pre-mock revision push
This term: weekly HL or SL foundation building
Mid-year joiners: gap-filling after a school move

contentBlocks.heading: How a Tutor Actually Gets Chosen for Your Child
contentBlocks.body:
Matching starts with specifics, not a general request for 'a good chemistry tutor.' A parent shares the student's grade — anywhere from Grade 1 to Grade 12 is supported on IB Gram, though Chemistry itself becomes relevant from the MYP sciences onward and turns into a defined DP subject in Grade 11 and 12. For DP students, the level matters immediately: HL and SL Chemistry share a core but diverge sharply in depth, especially around option topics and calculation-heavy problem sets, so a tutor comfortable teaching one is not automatically right for the other.

Next comes the actual gap. Some students need conceptual teaching from the start of a topic. Others already understand the chemistry but lose marks on IA structure, data processing or evaluating uncertainty — a different skill that calls for a tutor experienced in IA supervision rather than just subject knowledge. Assessment support on IB Gram covers this range: IA planning, EE mentoring for Chemistry-adjacent extended essays, TOK connections where relevant, school assignment help, and mock revision built around past-paper practice.

Only after grade, level and gap are clear does scheduling and mode enter the picture — whether home tutoring in a reachable Delhi pocket makes sense, or whether online tutoring opens up a wider pool of subject specialists. Getting this sequence right, rather than starting with 'who is available,' is what keeps the eventual match relevant instead of convenient.
items: Grade and DP level confirmed first (HL or SL)
Specific gap identified: concept, technique or IA/EE
Assessment need mapped: IA, EE, TOK, mocks or past papers
Mode decided last: home, online or hybrid

contentBlocks.heading: Math AA, Physics and the Rest of the DP Timetable
contentBlocks.body:
Chemistry rarely arrives alone. Delhi students on IB Gram most often pair Chemistry support with Math AA HL or Math AI HL, since calculation-heavy topics like equilibrium constants, buffer calculations and kinetics rest on comfort with logs and algebra that some students never fully settled in Grade 10. Physics is the next most common pairing — a student weak in one of the two DP sciences is frequently weak in both, since the underlying mathematical reasoning overlaps more than school timetables suggest.

Economics and English A show up for a different reason: not academic weakness, but time pressure. A student managing Chemistry HL alongside Economics IA research and an English A commentary is not short on ability, usually, but short on hours in the week. In these cases, the useful intervention is often not more Chemistry teaching but tighter, more efficient sessions — clear homework between classes, focused past-paper drilling instead of re-teaching, and realistic pacing that respects the other subjects competing for the same evening.

IB Gram's subject coverage in Delhi extends across this full DP science and humanities range, which matters because a family juggling two or three struggling subjects benefits from tutors who can coordinate rather than work in isolation, each assuming they have the student's undivided attention.

Math AI HL
Physics
Economics
English A

contentBlocks.heading: Chemistry's Place Across PYP, MYP and the Diploma
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram supports the Primary Years Programme for ages 3 to 12, the Middle Years Programme for ages 11 to 16, and the Diploma Programme for ages 16 to 19 — which in practice covers Delhi students from Grade 1 through Grade 12. Chemistry as a distinct, exam-facing subject really begins in the Middle Years Programme, where it sits inside integrated sciences before separating into its own discipline, and becomes fully defined only in the Diploma Programme.

A PYP student rarely needs a 'Chemistry tutor' in the formal sense; what helps at that stage is a tutor comfortable with inquiry-based science units and building curiosity rather than content mastery. MYP students start to meet real chemistry vocabulary — particle models, simple reactions, early lab reports — and this is often where a shaky foundation either gets caught or gets carried forward into the DP, where it becomes far more expensive to fix.

By the time a student reaches DP Chemistry, the subject has its own syllabus, its own HL and SL split, and its own IA. A tutor who has taught across this progression understands why a Grade 12 student's trouble with equilibrium sometimes traces back to a Grade 8 gap in mole concept that was never quite closed, and can decide whether to patch it quickly or rebuild it properly depending on how much time is left before May or November.
items: PYP (ages 3-12): inquiry-based science, not yet formal Chemistry
MYP (ages 11-16): integrated sciences, early lab and vocabulary building
DP (ages 16-19): full Chemistry HL/SL syllabus and IA
Grade 1 to Grade 12 supported overall on IB Gram

contentBlocks.heading: South and Central Delhi, and Where Travel Gets Harder
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring for IB Chemistry is most commonly arranged in Vasant Vihar, Greater Kailash, Saket and Chanakyapuri, where a reasonable concentration of IB and international-curriculum families makes a tutor's weekly travel worthwhile. Nearby pockets — Defence Colony, Hauz Khas, New Friends Colony, Panchsheel Park, Green Park and Jor Bagh — are also realistic for home visits, particularly when a family is open to a session time that avoids Delhi's worst traffic windows.

Beyond this belt, home tutoring becomes harder to sustain, not impossible but harder. A tutor who commits to a weekly slot in Chanakyapuri and another slot across the city on the same evening is setting up a schedule that traffic will eventually break. This is one honest limitation worth stating plainly: geography matters more for home tutoring than most marketing pages admit, and IB Gram would rather say so than promise a match that will not hold up after three weeks.

Families in Gurugram, Noida and Ghaziabad searching for IB Chemistry support are usually better served by online tutoring from the outset, since the subject specialist pool there is not meaningfully constrained by which side of Delhi they live on. Even within Delhi, plenty of families in the areas listed above choose online sessions anyway, once they realise a stronger HL specialist is available online than within reasonable driving distance.

Defence Colony and Hauz Khas nearby
New Friends Colony, Panchsheel Park, Green Park, Jor Bagh
Gurugram, Noida and Ghaziabad via online tutoring

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or a Mix — What Actually Fits
contentBlocks.body:
Delhi families tend to land on one of three arrangements. Full home tutoring, where a tutor visits weekly, works best for families in or near the South and central Delhi pockets already mentioned, and for younger students who benefit from someone physically present to keep focus. Full online tutoring works for everyone else, including families in Gurugram, Noida and Ghaziabad, and for any Delhi family prioritising a specific subject specialist over proximity — an HL Chemistry tutor who genuinely knows the option topics well is worth more than one who merely lives fifteen minutes away.

The third arrangement, hybrid, is what many Delhi families end up choosing without necessarily planning it that way: home tutoring for subjects where in-person explanation helps most, online for a subject like Chemistry where past-paper walkthroughs and screen-shared diagrams work perfectly well on a laptop. This matters practically — a whiteboard app with molecular structures and reaction mechanisms translates onto a screen more easily than a discussion-heavy English A commentary session.

Online tutoring on IB Gram is available across Delhi for every supported IB programme and subject, and it scales down to short revision cycles before a school mock as easily as it scales up to a longer weekly plan for a student rebuilding foundations from Grade 10 onward. Home tutoring availability, by contrast, depends on tutor location and is not guaranteed everywhere; it can be reviewed on a case-by-case basis once the family's area and schedule are known.
items: Home tutoring: best in South/central Delhi, good for younger students
Online tutoring: available citywide, best for subject specialists
Hybrid: common default for multi-subject households
Short revision cycles or longer weekly plans, both supported online

contentBlocks.heading: The School Context Behind a Delhi Chemistry Request
contentBlocks.body:
Delhi's IB Chemistry demand is closely tied to a handful of school clusters. Chanakyapuri is home to schools such as The British School New Delhi and the American Embassy School, both drawing embassy and diplomatic families whose posting cycles often do not align neatly with the DP's two-year structure — a student might join mid-way through Grade 11 Chemistry HL with a syllabus gap that needs mapping before anything else happens. Saket, meanwhile, is associated with DPS International Saket, drawing a different mix of resident and transitioning families.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. What matters for tutoring purposes is not the school's name but its assessment calendar and internal pacing: some schools front-load organic chemistry earlier than others, some run internal mocks in December rather than February, and a tutor who has worked with students from a similar school calendar adjusts faster than one starting cold.

For a family whose child attends one of these schools, or a school with a comparable IB Chemistry pacing, the practical benefit of mentioning the school during matching is calendar alignment, not credential-chasing. It lets a tutor plan backward from the actual submission and mock dates the student is facing, rather than a generic term structure that may not match the school's own rhythm at all.

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Tutor Is Recommended
contentBlocks.body:
Before a Chemistry tutor is suggested to a Delhi family, a few things are checked rather than assumed. Subject background is confirmed — whether the tutor has taught DP Chemistry specifically, at what level, and for how many exam cycles, since familiarity with the May and November 2026 assessment structure is different from general chemistry teaching experience picked up outside the IB system. Where a tutor claims IA supervision experience, that claim is looked at against what IA support actually involves: helping a student choose a researchable question, plan a method with enough data points, and evaluate systematic error properly, not simply reviewing a finished draft for grammar.

Availability is verified honestly rather than optimistically. If a tutor says they can take a Tuesday evening home slot in Greater Kailash, that is checked against their existing weekly commitments, not just their general willingness. This is also why availability across the platform is described conditionally — a tutor's schedule can change, and a suggested match is always subject to tutor availability at the point a family actually reaches out.

None of this produces a guarantee about outcomes, and IB Gram does not claim one. What the verification step produces is a reasonable basis for a first session: a tutor whose background actually matches what the student needs, rather than a name pulled from a general list because they were free.

IA supervision experience checked against real IA criteria
Stated availability checked against actual weekly commitments

contentBlocks.heading: Four Weeks In: What Should Be Different
contentBlocks.body:
A first session with an IB Chemistry tutor should do more than introduce the syllabus. It should identify, specifically, where the student's understanding breaks down — a topic like chemical equilibrium might reveal that the student can balance an equation fine but freezes the moment Le Chatelier's principle is applied to a real scenario. A tutor worth continuing with will usually flag two or three such gaps by the end of session one, not a vague 'needs more practice.'

By the end of four weeks, a parent should be able to see something concrete: fewer errors on a specific type of calculation, a completed IA research question where there was none before, or a mock score that reflects the topics actually covered rather than the whole syllabus. If none of that has happened, that is worth raising directly rather than waiting out the term hoping it improves on its own.

Mismatches happen, and pretending otherwise would not help anyone. A tutor who teaches well but at a pace too fast for a particular student, or whose home-visit slot keeps clashing with Delhi traffic, is a mismatch worth correcting rather than tolerating. IB Gram treats a tutor change mid-term as a normal part of getting the match right, not as a failure. The goal is a tutor the student will actually keep working with through May or November 2026, not the first name suggested.
items: Session one: 2-3 specific gaps identified, not a general overview
Week four: a visible, specific improvement, not just more confidence
Mismatch on pace, style or schedule can be corrected mid-term
Goal is a tutor the student keeps through the exam session

contentBlocks.heading: Starting This Week, This Month or This Term
contentBlocks.body:
Starting is deliberately simple: share the student's grade, HL or SL level if they are in the Diploma Programme, the specific gap — a topic, an IA stage, a mock score — and whether home tutoring in a South or central Delhi pocket is realistic or online suits the family better. From there, a tutor match can usually be proposed quickly, subject to availability, and a first session scheduled around school timings rather than around the tutor's convenience.

Families under time pressure — a mock next week, an IA draft due in ten days — should say so upfront, since it changes what the first session covers. Families with more runway can use the same process to set up a steady weekly rhythm through to the May or November 2026 exam session, built around a syllabus review rather than emergency triage.

There is no obligation attached to asking. A parent can describe the situation, see what matching looks like for that specific case, and decide from there whether to proceed. For a subject like Chemistry, where a gap in one topic can quietly undermine three others months later, the earlier this conversation happens relative to the exam date, the more options remain on the table. Even a late start, honestly, still has a place: it will simply have narrower goals, focused on the highest-value topics rather than full syllabus coverage.
items: Share grade, HL/SL level and the specific gap
State the timeline: this week, this month or this term
Choose home (South/central Delhi), online, or hybrid
First session scheduled around school timings

faqs.question: How much does an IB Chemistry tutor in Delhi cost?
faqs.answer: Fees vary by tutor experience, HL versus SL level, and whether sessions are home-based or online — home tutoring in areas like Vasant Vihar or Saket typically costs more per session than online tutoring, given travel time factored into a tutor's schedule. IB Gram does not publish a fixed rate because a first-year MYP science tutor and a tutor with several DP Chemistry HL cohorts behind them are not comparable services. The honest answer is to describe the grade, level and gap first; a realistic fee range follows from that, not the other way round.

faqs.question: Is online IB Chemistry tutoring actually effective, or is home tutoring always better?
faqs.answer: Online tutoring works well for Chemistry specifically because much of the subject — diagrams, reaction mechanisms, past-paper walkthroughs — translates cleanly onto a shared screen. It is not automatically worse than home tutoring; for many Delhi families, especially outside South and central Delhi, it is the more practical option and often gives access to a stronger HL specialist. Home tutoring still helps younger students or those who lose focus without someone present. Neither mode is universally better; the right choice depends on the student's age, the topic, and how far a tutor would otherwise need to travel.

faqs.question: What if the tutor and my child are not a good match?
faqs.answer: This happens sometimes, and it is treated as normal rather than as a problem to hide from. A pacing mismatch, a teaching style the student does not respond to, or a scheduling clash that keeps disrupting sessions are all valid reasons to request a change. IB Gram would rather a family raise this in week two than continue for a full term hoping it resolves itself. A tutor change mid-term does not restart the process from zero — the grade, level and identified gaps carry over, so the next match starts from what is already known about the student.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help specifically with the IB Chemistry Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Yes — IA planning is part of the assessment support IB Gram covers for Chemistry. This typically means helping a student choose a researchable question, design a method that will generate enough usable data, and evaluate sources of error properly rather than listing them generically. It does not mean writing or rewriting the IA for the student, which would defeat its purpose and risk the school's own authenticity checks. A tutor's role is to strengthen the student's own investigation and writing, particularly around the analysis and evaluation sections where most marks are typically lost.

faqs.question: My child is in South Delhi — can we get a home tutor, or is it online only?
faqs.answer: Home tutoring may be possible for families in or near Vasant Vihar, Greater Kailash, Saket, Chanakyapuri and nearby pockets like Defence Colony or Hauz Khas, depending on which tutors are available and how their existing weekly schedule sits. It is not guaranteed for every request in these areas, since it depends on tutor availability at the time, but it is realistic enough to ask for directly. Families slightly further out, or in NCR cities like Gurugram, Noida or Ghaziabad, are generally better matched with online tutoring from the start rather than waiting on a home-tutor slot that may not open up.

faqs.question: We're starting late — is it worth getting a tutor two months before May 2026 finals?
faqs.answer: It is worth it, but the goals need to be realistic. Two months is enough time to close specific, well-identified gaps — a shaky topic like equilibrium calculations, or IA sections losing easy marks — and to build strong past-paper technique. It is not enough time to rebuild a syllabus's worth of foundational understanding from scratch. An honest tutor working on this timeline will prioritise the highest-value topics and exam technique over full coverage, and will say so plainly rather than promising to fix everything before the exam session arrives.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram work with students who are new to the IB system, not just DP Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Yes. IB Gram supports the full range from Grade 1 through Grade 12, covering the Primary Years Programme, Middle Years Programme and Diploma Programme. A student moving into an IB-curriculum school in Delhi mid-year, perhaps from a different board, often needs help adjusting to inquiry-based assessment and IB-style questioning before Chemistry content becomes the main issue. This adjustment period is treated as its own kind of support, distinct from straightforward subject tutoring, and is factored into how a tutor is matched for a newly-arrived student.

faqs.question: Is my child's school affiliated with IB Gram?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with any school, including schools mentioned here such as The British School New Delhi, the American Embassy School or DPS International Saket, unless specifically stated otherwise. Knowing a student's school helps a tutor understand likely pacing and assessment timing, since schools within the same city do not all follow an identical internal calendar, but it does not imply any formal relationship between IB Gram and the school itself.

faqs.question: How do I know if my child needs HL or SL Chemistry support?
faqs.answer: The DP subject choice is usually already made by the school or the student before tutoring is arranged, so this is less often a live question — but the support needed differs sharply by level. HL adds option-topic depth and more demanding calculation work across Papers 1 and 2, and generally needs a tutor with recent HL teaching experience rather than SL-only background. If a student is struggling significantly at HL, that is sometimes a conversation about the tutor's approach before it is a conversation about switching levels, which is a school decision, not a tutoring one.

faqs.question: What happens after four weeks if there's no real improvement?
faqs.answer: That is exactly when it should be raised, not ignored. A visible sign of progress by week four — fewer errors on a specific calculation type, a completed IA question, more confident past-paper attempts — is a reasonable thing to expect and to ask about directly. If it has not happened, the likely causes are worth naming plainly: wrong pace, insufficient session frequency, or a gap that turned out deeper than first assessed. IB Gram treats this as a signal to adjust the plan or the tutor, not a reason to wait out the rest of the term hoping it changes.

If a student is struggling significantly at HL, that is sometimes a conversation about the tutor's approach before it is a conversation about switching levels, which is a school decision, not a tutoring one.

mainEntity.name: What happens after four weeks if there's no real improvement?

acceptedAnswer.text: That is exactly when it should be raised, not ignored. A visible sign of progress by week four — fewer errors on a specific calculation type, a completed IA question, more confident past-paper attempts — is a reasonable thing to expect and to ask about directly. If it has not happened, the likely causes are worth naming plainly: wrong pace, insufficient session frequency, or a gap that turned out deeper than first assessed. IB Gram treats this as a signal to adjust the plan or the tutor, not a reason to wait out the rest of the term hoping it changes.

introSummary: Searching for an IB Economics tutor in Delhi usually means one of two things: a Grade 11 student who needs HL or SL concepts explained clearly, or a Grade 12 student staring at an IA deadline with a research question that does not quite work yet. Delhi families also deal with a third problem most searches ignore — traffic. A tutor who is excellent but lives ninety minutes away by car is not always the right match.
