contentBlocks.heading: What Parents Search For, And What Actually Moves The Grade
contentBlocks.body:
Type 'IB Economics tutor in Delhi' into a search bar and pages promising the best tutor in the city show up everywhere. No one can prove that claim, and most parents know it. What actually changes a grade in IB Economics is narrower: a tutor who can tell HL and SL syllabus depth apart, who reads an IA draft and points out exactly which paragraph is descriptive instead of evaluative, and who has marked enough Paper 1 and Paper 2 responses to know where students lose easy marks on definitions and diagrams.

Delhi adds a layer that generic searches skip. Demand here comes from embassy families, international school households, and students who commute across NCR — Gurugram, Noida and Ghaziabad are among the cities Delhi families often move between for school and coaching schedules. A tutor who is strong on paper but lives ninety minutes from a South Delhi flat by evening traffic will not keep a Tuesday 6pm slot reliably. So the search that starts as 'best IB Economics tutor' should really end as 'which tutor understands HL/SL depth and can actually turn up, on time, most weeks.'

This page covers what IB Economics tutoring looks like across Grade 1 to Grade 12 support at IB Gram, which Delhi areas support home visits, how IA and EE mentoring fits alongside subject teaching, and what a family should check before starting.
items: HL and SL syllabus depth are not interchangeable
IA feedback needs to flag descriptive vs evaluative writing
Paper 1 and Paper 2 technique explains most lost marks
Location affects reliability more than Delhi parents expect
Grade 1 to Grade 12 support means matching changes by age

contentBlocks.heading: Where IB Economics Fits Across the Delhi Programme Range
contentBlocks.body:
IB Economics itself belongs to the Diploma Programme, the stage built for ages 16 to 19, and it can be taken at Higher Level or Standard Level. That distinction matters early: HL asks for more depth in areas like the Keynesian multiplier and exchange rate systems, while SL covers the same four sections at a lighter pace. Choosing HL without a clear reason for it is one of the more avoidable mistakes Delhi families make in Grade 11.

IB Gram supports Grade 1 through Grade 12, which covers Primary Years Programme learners aged 3 to 12, Middle Years Programme students aged 11 to 16, and Diploma Programme students aged 16 to 19. That range matters for Economics families in a specific way. A Grade 9 or 10 student in the Middle Years Programme studying Individuals and Societies can get a head start on the thinking Economics later demands — reading a data set, weighing a trade-off, writing an argument that takes a stance instead of describing both sides. Families sometimes book that groundwork a year before DP subject selection, rather than waiting until Grade 11 to discover their child finds economic reasoning unfamiliar. Younger siblings in the Primary Years Programme are supported too, though the tutoring there looks nothing like Economics coaching — it is closer to building study habits and subject confidence early.
items: Economics sits in the Diploma Programme (ages 16-19), at HL or SL
HL adds depth in areas like exchange rate systems and the multiplier
MYP Individuals and Societies work can prepare students for DP Economics
IB Gram supports Grade 1 to Grade 12 overall, not DP only
Primary Years Programme support looks like study skills, not subject coaching

contentBlocks.heading: Which Delhi Neighbourhoods Home Tutoring Actually Reaches
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring, where it is feasible at all, tends to work best in South Delhi and central Delhi. Vasant Vihar, Greater Kailash, Saket and Chanakyapuri come up often because they sit close to several international schools and to each other, which keeps a tutor's evening schedule realistic instead of a single 90-minute trip eating an entire slot. Defence Colony, Hauz Khas, New Friends Colony, Panchsheel Park, Green Park and Jor Bagh fall into the same practical radius — a tutor already teaching in Saket can often extend to Panchsheel Park or Green Park without the visit becoming unsustainable for either side.

Home tutoring is not guaranteed everywhere in Delhi. Whether a home visit works depends on the tutor's own location, the family's exact address within these pockets, and how timing lines up with school hours and Delhi's evening traffic. A flat in outer Delhi asking for a 7pm weekday slot with a South Delhi specialist is a harder match than the same request from Greater Kailash. This is where online tutoring earns its place, not as a fallback but as the more reliable option for many Delhi families — it removes the commute variable and opens up tutors who would never be reachable by car within a school evening. For Economics specifically, where the actual teaching is discussion and diagram work rather than lab equipment, the online format loses very little compared to sitting in the same room.
items: Vasant Vihar, Greater Kailash, Saket and Chanakyapuri: most workable for home visits
Defence Colony, Hauz Khas, New Friends Colony, Panchsheel Park, Green Park, Jor Bagh: same practical radius
Outer Delhi addresses are harder to match for evening home slots
Online tutoring removes the commute variable entirely
Economics teaching is discussion-based, so video loses little versus in-person

contentBlocks.heading: Economics Alongside The Other Subjects Delhi DP Students Juggle
contentBlocks.body:
Economics rarely sits alone on a Delhi DP student's plate. Most students taking it are also managing Math AA HL or Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry or English A, and the specific combination changes how tutoring should be scheduled and taught. A student pairing Economics with Math AA HL usually has stronger quantitative instincts and can move faster through elasticity calculations and exchange rate mechanics, but may need more push on the extended written analysis that Paper 2 and the IA reward. A student coming from Math AI HL or leaning on English A as a strength often writes fluently but needs more structured practice translating a diagram into an argument.

The IA is where subject-specific coaching matters most. It asks for a real-world article, a research question narrow enough to answer in 2,000 words, and evaluation that goes beyond restating theory. Delhi tutors working across Economics IA drafts typically flag three recurring problems: research questions that are really just descriptions, diagrams included without being used in the argument, and evaluation sections written as an afterthought rather than planned from the first draft. TOK support sometimes intersects here too, since economics as a way of knowing is a natural TOK link for students who want one.

None of this replaces school teaching. A tutor's job is to fill the specific gap — a shaky diagram, an underdeveloped evaluation, a Paper 3 data-response habit that is not yet automatic — rather than re-teach the whole syllabus from scratch.

IA needs a narrow research question, not a broad topic
Diagrams must be used in the argument, not just included
Evaluation should be planned from the first draft, not added last
Economics can serve as a TOK way-of-knowing link for students who want one

contentBlocks.heading: Schools In The Picture, Without Pretending To Be Part Of Them
contentBlocks.body:
Families researching IB Economics tutoring in Delhi often mention specific schools when describing what they need, and it helps to be direct about this: IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. The British School New Delhi and the American Embassy School, both in Chanakyapuri, and DPS International Saket in Saket, are examples of the kind of DP cohort context Delhi tutors are used to working around — school calendars, mock exam windows, and the particular way each school sequences Economics topics across Grade 11 and Grade 12.

Knowing a student's school does not mean a tutor has seen that school's exact syllabus pack or internal assessment schedule. What it does mean is a tutor can ask better questions in the first session: which topics has the school already covered, when are internal mocks scheduled relative to May or November exam sessions, and whether the school's own Economics teacher has given feedback on IA drafts that a tutor should build on rather than contradict. A tutor who ignores what the school has already told a student, and simply reteaches from a personal framework, usually creates confusion rather than clarity.

This matters more in Chanakyapuri and Saket specifically, where several DP cohorts sit close together geographically but follow different school calendars and different internal deadlines. A plan built around 'DP Economics students in general' is weaker than one built around this student's school timeline, exam board expectations for HL or SL, and what has already been taught.

The British School New Delhi and American Embassy School: both in Chanakyapuri
DPS International Saket: in Saket
Tutors ask about school-specific mock timing, not just the syllabus
A student's own school feedback on IA drafts should guide tutoring, not get overridden

contentBlocks.heading: How A Tutor Actually Gets Matched To Your Child
contentBlocks.body:
Matching starts with specifics, not a general request for 'a good Economics tutor.' IB Gram asks for the grade, whether the student is on HL or SL, what the student is stuck on right now — IA structure, Paper 3 data response, a weak macroeconomics unit — and what schedule the family can actually sustain across a normal Delhi week, including school hours and any existing commitments. That last part gets skipped in most searches, and it is often the reason a technically excellent tutor fails to work out.

From there, a shortlist is built around subject background and exam-board familiarity rather than general teaching experience. A tutor recommended for IB Economics has been checked for depth in the actual DP syllabus — HL and SL distinctions, IA assessment criteria, Paper 1, 2 and 3 formats — not just an economics degree and general goodwill. The first session is diagnostic rather than instructional: reviewing where the student's understanding actually sits, looking at any existing IA draft or recent test, and agreeing what the next four weeks will focus on.

Week four is a checkpoint IB Gram takes seriously. A parent should be able to see something concrete by then — a clearer IA research question, fewer basic errors on diagram labelling, more confidence attempting Paper 2 essay questions unprompted. If that is not happening, the honest response is not to keep going regardless. It is to look at whether the tutor is the right subject fit, whether the schedule is actually being kept, or whether the student needs a different kind of support altogether before more sessions are booked.
items: Matching starts from grade, HL/SL, specific gap, and realistic schedule
Tutors are checked for DP syllabus depth, not just a degree
First session is diagnostic: review draft IA or recent test, not a lecture
Week 4 should show a visible, specific change
No improvement by week 4 means reviewing fit, not continuing blindly

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online Or Hybrid: What Actually Suits An Economics Student
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring works best when it can be sustained without strain — a fixed evening slot, a realistic distance, a subject where sitting across a table adds something a screen does not. For a younger student building basic economic reasoning for the first time, being in the same room can help, especially when a tutor is walking through a diagram by hand and checking body language for confusion that a student would never type into a chat box.

Online tutoring suits Economics unusually well for a different reason: the subject is argument and analysis, not lab work or handwriting practice, so a shared screen with an annotated diagram does almost everything a printed page would. It also opens up tutors who specialise in IA mentoring or Paper 3 data response but do not live anywhere near South or central Delhi, which matters when the actual gap is subject expertise rather than proximity. Families across Delhi, not just the areas suited to home visits, can use online tutoring for short revision cycles before school mocks or for a longer weekly plan aimed at rebuilding foundations.

Many Delhi families land on a hybrid pattern without planning it that way: home sessions where travel is genuinely realistic, online sessions when a stronger subject specialist matters more than being in the room, or the reverse split during intense IA weeks when a student needs face-to-face structure to actually finish a draft. There is no single right ratio. What matters is picking the mode for the actual constraint in front of you that week, not defaulting to whichever mode was used the first time.
items: Home tutoring: best with a fixed slot and a realistic distance
Online tutoring: shared screen handles diagram-based teaching well
Online opens access to IA and Paper 3 specialists outside Delhi's south/central belt
Short online revision cycles before mocks are common
Hybrid patterns often shift week to week rather than staying fixed

contentBlocks.heading: What IB Gram Will Not Promise You
contentBlocks.body:
A page like this could list a tutor count, a set of average grade improvements, or a handful of glowing parent quotes. IB Gram does not, because none of that is verifiable in a way that means anything to your family specifically. What one tutor achieved with one student in one school context does not transfer as a promise to a different Grade 12 student in Chanakyapuri working on a different IA question under a different school's internal deadline.

What IB Gram will say plainly: it is an independent tutoring platform, not affiliated with the IB Organization, Cambridge, Pearson Edexcel, or any specific school unless that is stated directly on a school's own page. It does not set exam grades, does not have influence over IA moderation, and cannot guarantee a 6 or a 7. Anyone claiming they can guarantee an IB grade is telling you something that is not true, because final grades are set by the IB Organization's own moderation and marking process, not by any tutoring provider.

What IB Gram can commit to is narrower and more useful: matching based on actual subject depth and schedule fit, availability that is described honestly as conditional rather than promised as unlimited, and a process for handling it when a match is not working rather than pretending that never happens. Availability for home tutoring in South Delhi and Chanakyapuri-area pockets, for instance, depends on which tutors are free that term and is never guaranteed in advance. That is a smaller claim than 'the best tutor in Delhi.' It also happens to be the honest one.

Independent platform, not affiliated with IB Organization, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel
No influence over IA moderation or final grade-setting
Availability is conditional on tutor free terms, not unlimited
A mismatch gets handled, not ignored

contentBlocks.heading: Checks Run Before A Tutor Ever Meets Your Child
contentBlocks.body:
Before a tutor is recommended for IB Economics in Delhi, the check is specific to the subject rather than a general teaching credential. That means confirming actual DP Economics experience — not adjacent commerce or business teaching mistaken for the same thing — familiarity with the command terms IB examiners actually use (define, explain, evaluate, to what extent), and comfort with both HL and SL demands where a tutor claims both.

IA mentoring is checked separately from subject teaching ability, because the two skills do not always travel together. A tutor can explain macroeconomics clearly and still give vague, generic feedback on an IA draft if they have not actually mentored students through the specific assessment criteria examiners use. IB Gram looks for tutors who can point at a paragraph and say precisely why it reads as descriptive rather than evaluative, not tutors who only offer encouragement.

Scheduling reliability gets checked too, particularly for Delhi's home tutoring pockets, because a tutor who is brilliant but unreliable across a South Delhi commute causes more damage to a student's confidence than a tutor who is merely good but consistent. None of this produces a public score or a star rating, since ratings built on a handful of self-selected reviews are easy to game and tell a parent very little. What it produces instead is a smaller, more relevant shortlist for your specific request — grade, level, subject gap, and area — rather than a long list you have to filter yourself.
items: DP Economics experience checked specifically, not general commerce teaching
Familiarity with IB command terms: define, explain, evaluate, to what extent
IA mentoring ability checked separately from subject teaching
Scheduling reliability matters as much as subject knowledge for home tutoring
No public star ratings; shortlist is matched to your specific request instead

contentBlocks.heading: Starting With One Practical Conversation, Not A Signup Form
contentBlocks.body:
Starting is meant to be simple: describe the grade, HL or SL, what is actually going wrong right now, and whether home tutoring in a South or central Delhi pocket is realistic for your schedule or online tutoring makes more sense. From that, IB Gram puts together a shortlist based on subject depth and fit rather than sending the first available name.

There is no obligation to commit to a long-term plan before knowing whether the match works. A short revision block before a school mock is a reasonable way to start for a student who mainly needs Paper 2 or Paper 3 technique tightened up. A longer weekly plan makes more sense for a student rebuilding foundations across a full HL syllabus, or working through an IA from research question to final draft over several weeks.

If May 2026 or November 2026 is the target exam session, timing matters more than it might seem. Four months of steady, focused sessions on Paper 3 data response and IA revision usually does more than six months of unfocused general coverage. Whatever situation your child is in — new to the subject, mid-syllabus, weeks from a mock, or drafting an IA under deadline pressure — start with the specific problem, not the search term, and the right match follows from there.

Home vs online decided by realistic schedule, not preference alone
Short revision blocks work before a mock
Longer weekly plans suit full-syllabus or IA rebuilding work
May 2026 and November 2026 sessions set the timing math

faqs.question: How much does an IB Economics tutor in Delhi cost?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the tutor's experience, whether sessions are HL or SL, and whether you choose home tutoring in a South or central Delhi pocket or online tutoring, which is often more flexible on scheduling. IB Gram does not publish one fixed number because a Grade 9 introductory session and a Grade 12 IA-mentoring session with a specialist tutor are not the same service. Ask for a clear per-session or per-month rate before the first session, confirm what it covers, and treat any number quoted without knowing the grade or level as unreliable.

faqs.question: Can we switch tutors if the first match is not working?
faqs.answer: Yes. A mismatch is not unusual, and continuing with a tutor who is not the right subject or personality fit wastes time your child does not have, especially close to a May or November exam session. Tell IB Gram specifically what is not working — pace, communication style, depth on HL content, IA feedback quality — rather than a general 'it is not working,' because specific feedback produces a better second match. Switching does not mean starting over from zero; a new tutor should be briefed on what was already covered so sessions do not repeat ground unnecessarily.

faqs.question: Does online IB Economics tutoring actually work, or is home tutoring always better?
faqs.answer: For Economics specifically, online works close to as well as in person, because the teaching is discussion, diagrams and essay structure rather than lab work or handwriting drills. What matters more than the format is whether the tutor annotates a shared screen clearly, checks understanding actively, and reviews written work in detail between sessions. Home tutoring has a real edge for younger students needing more direct attention, or when a family finds video sessions harder to keep focused. Neither mode is automatically better for every student.

faqs.question: My child is starting IB Economics HL in Grade 11 with no background in economics at all. Is that too late?
faqs.answer: No, Grade 11 is a normal starting point for HL Economics since most schools introduce it fresh at Diploma Programme level regardless of prior exposure. What matters is pace early on: getting comfortable with basic diagrams and terminology in the first few weeks so later units in international and development economics do not compound confusion. Students with no prior background typically need more structured sessions for the first month, then settle into a normal rhythm once core vocabulary is solid. Waiting until Grade 12 to fix a shaky foundation is harder, since IA work and Paper 3 practice then compete for the same time.

faqs.question: Is IB Economics tutoring available in Gurugram, Noida or Ghaziabad, or only inside Delhi?
faqs.answer: Online IB Economics tutoring works the same way regardless of which NCR city a family is in, since the format does not depend on a Delhi address. Home tutoring is different — it is centred on Delhi's South and central pockets like Vasant Vihar, Greater Kailash, Saket and Chanakyapuri, and a home tutor already committed to that radius is unlikely to also take on a Gurugram or Noida address reliably. Families in Gurugram, Noida or Ghaziabad who want a Delhi-based subject specialist should plan on online sessions rather than assuming a home visit is realistic across that distance.

faqs.question: What exactly happens in the first IB Economics session?
faqs.answer: The first session is diagnostic, not a lecture on economic theory. A tutor reviews recent test scripts, an existing IA draft if there is one, and school notes to see where the actual gaps sit — a weak macroeconomics unit, shaky diagram labelling, or an IA research question that is too broad. From that, the tutor and student agree what the next few weeks will target and roughly how progress will be checked, whether that is a mock Paper 2 essay, a revised IA introduction, or a short diagnostic quiz on definitions. Parents are usually given a short summary of what was found and what is planned next.

faqs.question: What if there is no real progress after a month of IB Economics tutoring?
faqs.answer: That should not happen quietly. Week four is meant to show something concrete — a clearer IA research question, fewer errors on standard diagram labelling, more confidence attempting Paper 2 or Paper 3 questions without prompting. If none of that is visible, the right response is not simply to add more sessions and hope. Raise it directly, look at whether the tutor is the right subject fit, whether the agreed schedule was actually kept on both sides, and whether the student needs a different kind of support, such as more foundational work before exam technique makes sense. A stalled month is information, not a reason to stay quiet.

faqs.question: Do tutors help with the IB Economics Internal Assessment, and how is that different from regular tutoring?
faqs.answer: Yes, IA mentoring is treated as a distinct skill from teaching the syllabus. A tutor helping with the IA works on narrowing a research question to something answerable in the word limit, checking that a chosen article and diagram actually support the argument, and pushing the evaluation section beyond a summary of both sides. This is different from weekly subject tutoring, which focuses on building understanding of microeconomics, macroeconomics, international and development economics topics for tests and exams. Many Delhi students use both — regular sessions through the term and a concentrated block of IA-specific sessions closer to the school's internal deadline.

faqs.question: How do I know a tutor actually understands the IB Economics syllabus and not just general economics?
faqs.answer: Ask direct questions before committing: whether they can explain the difference between HL and SL content, whether they know the current IA assessment criteria, and whether they can describe what Paper 1, Paper 2 and Paper 3 each actually test. A tutor with real DP experience answers these specifically and quickly; one without it tends to talk in general economics terms — GDP, inflation, demand curves — without connecting them to how the IB actually assesses the subject. IB Gram checks this before recommending a tutor, but asking it yourself in an introductory call is a reasonable extra check, and a fair question to expect a clear answer to.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help just before the May 2026 or November 2026 exam session, or is it too late by then?
faqs.answer: It depends heavily on how much time is left and what exactly is weak. A few weeks before May 2026 or November 2026 is genuinely too late to fix a shaky HL foundation from scratch, but it is realistic timing for focused Paper 3 data-response practice, past-paper technique, and tightening up an already-drafted IA. Being honest about what a short window can and cannot do matters more than promising a turnaround. Students six to eight weeks out from their session usually get the most from concentrated past-paper practice and targeted feedback rather than fresh topic teaching at that stage.

A tutor with real DP experience answers these specifically and quickly; one without it tends to talk in general economics terms — GDP, inflation, demand curves — without connecting them to how the IB actually assesses the subject. Students six to eight weeks out from their session usually get the most from concentrated past-paper practice and targeted feedback rather than fresh topic teaching at that stage.

introSummary: If you're searching for an IB Math AA HL tutor in Delhi right now, the honest answer depends on your timeline. Grade 12 students heading into the May 2026 exam session need past-paper practice and proof technique locked in well before mocks in December or January; starting in August still leaves room to close gaps. contentBlocks.heading: What's Due This Term, and How Late Is Too Late to Start
contentBlocks.body: Delhi's IB calendar doesn't run on one clock. Some schools finish their internal assessments by October; others push IA and coursework deadlines into December, right before mocks begin in January. For Math AA HL specifically, the syllabus front-loads calculus and functions in Grade 11, then spends Grade 12 layering proof, vectors and statistics on top of a foundation that either holds or doesn't. If your child is heading into the May 2026 session, August through October is the realistic window to fix conceptual gaps before revision has to take over. Starting in November still works, but it narrows the plan to targeted paper practice rather than rebuilding fundamentals. Grade 11 families aiming at November 2026 have more room, though many wait too long simply because the deadline feels distant. Waiting until after the first internal exam, when a low grade forces the conversation, is common in Delhi and usually recoverable, but it does mean fewer sessions to work with and less time for the IA to develop properly. A tutor search that starts now, even a slow one, still beats a search that starts in a panic six weeks before mocks. That's the honest trade-off worth naming before anything else.

Defence Colony, Hauz Khas, New Friends Colony, Panchsheel Park, Green Park and Jor Bagh come up often too, usually from parents comparing a home tutor against an online one before deciding. Outside these areas, Delhi's traffic makes a weekly home commitment hard to sustain for a tutor covering multiple students, so online tutoring tends to be the more dependable option, and it's available across the city regardless of postcode. Families in Gurugram, Noida and Ghaziabad searching for IB support are usually pointed to the same specialist pool online rather than a separate one, since strong Math AA HL tutors are not evenly distributed across NCR. None of this is a hard rule. A tutor who lives near Saket and a student in Vasant Vihar might make a home arrangement work even outside the core list, subject to the tutor's schedule and travel comfort. The honest guidance is: ask about your specific street before assuming either way.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Sessions, Online Sessions, or Both
contentBlocks.body: Not every family needs to choose one mode and stick with it. Hybrid support - a fortnightly home session for accountability plus weekly online sessions for pace - is common among Delhi parents who want a tutor physically present occasionally without paying for the travel time on every visit. Home tutoring works best when a student needs someone sitting beside them through a problem, particularly for younger MYP students still building study habits, or for HL students who freeze up during proof questions and need real-time correction. Online tutoring, by contrast, is often the better choice for Math AA HL specifically, because the strongest subject specialists - the ones who genuinely know where AA HL students lose marks on Paper 3 - are not always based near your home, and video tutoring with a shared whiteboard handles calculus workings perfectly well. It also survives Delhi's traffic and unpredictable school timings better than a fixed home slot does. Where home tutoring struggles is scheduling: a tutor stuck in traffic loses ten minutes of a sixty-minute session, and that adds up over a term. Online sessions start on time. The honest recommendation is to pick based on what the subject and the student actually need, not on which mode sounds more serious.

contentBlocks.heading: The Math AA HL Syllabus, Unit by Unit
contentBlocks.body: Math AA HL is not just 'harder Math AI.' The two courses diverge early: AA leans into proof, algebraic manipulation and calculus depth, where AI stays closer to applied, calculator-driven problem solving. A tutor who is strong in one is not automatically strong in the other, and Delhi parents sometimes discover this only after a term of slow progress. Good AA HL tutoring works through the syllabus in layers - functions and algebra first, then calculus, then vectors and complex numbers, then statistics and probability as the smaller but still exam-relevant unit. Paper 3 preparation, the investigative paper unique to HL, needs separate attention closer to exams; it rewards structured problem-solving over memorised methods, and most students only get comfortable with it after working through several past papers under timed conditions. If your child's IA is in Math, or if Math feeds into an Economics or Physics IA, a tutor who understands IB's assessment criteria for exploration and mathematical communication is worth more than one who only drills exam technique. Delhi families are also tutoring alongside Math AA HL in Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A, and TOK or EE mentoring where relevant, so scheduling one subject rarely happens in isolation from the rest of a student's term.

contentBlocks.heading: How a Match Gets Made, From Intake Call to Week Four
contentBlocks.body: Matching starts with a short intake call, not a form that disappears into a database. A parent describes the student's current grade, target session (May or November 2026), school syllabus pace and any specific weak topics - vectors, proof, whichever unit is causing trouble this term. From there, two or three tutors whose subject background and HL teaching experience fit the brief are shortlisted, with availability checked against the family's actual weekday schedule rather than an ideal one. The first session with the chosen tutor is diagnostic: working through a recent test or past paper together to see exactly where marks are being lost, not a generic 'getting to know you' chat. That diagnostic shapes the plan for the following weeks. By the end of week four, a parent should be able to point to something concrete - a topic that used to trip the student up now handled correctly, an IA draft with structure it didn't have before, or at minimum a clearer sense of what still needs work and why. If a match isn't working after a fair trial, the honest answer is to say so and switch, not to keep paying for a relationship that isn't producing results. That flexibility is built into how sessions are booked, not an afterthought.

contentBlocks.heading: Support Across the Full IB Journey, Not Just DP
contentBlocks.body: Most searches for a Math AA HL tutor come from Diploma Programme families, but the platform covers Grade 1 through Grade 12, and the earlier stages matter more than they get credit for. PYP support, for ages 3 to 12, is less about subject drilling and more about building the inquiry habits and number sense that make later IB work manageable - a student who struggled with fractions in Grade 4 often struggles with algebra in Grade 9 for the same underlying reason. MYP, ages 11 to 16, is where subject-specific gaps in Math or Science start to show up clearly, and it's also where many families first request a tutor for structured assignment support rather than open-ended homework help. By the time a student reaches DP at 16, choosing between AA and AI, HL and SL, is a decision worth getting right early, because switching levels mid-course is possible but costly in lost time. A tutor who has taught across these stages tends to explain concepts differently than one who has only ever taught exam technique to Grade 12 students - they can trace a current gap back to where it actually started, which is often two or three years earlier than the parent assumes.

faqs.question: How is IB Math AA HL different from Math AI HL, and does it matter for tutoring?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it's worth getting the tutor match right for it. AA HL builds around proof, algebraic rigor and calculus theory, while AI HL is more applied and calculator-dependent, closer to statistics and modelling. A tutor who has taught AI extensively isn't automatically strong at AA's proof-based Paper 3, and vice versa. Before booking, mention specifically that your child is in AA HL, not just 'IB Math,' so the shortlist reflects tutors with real HL-level calculus and proof teaching experience rather than general Math tutoring background.

faqs.question: Is home tutoring realistic if we live in Greater Kailash or Saket but our preferred tutor is elsewhere in Delhi?
faqs.answer: It depends on the tutor's own travel radius. Greater Kailash and Saket get steady home-tutoring requests, so there's usually reasonable choice within a manageable travel distance, but a tutor based in, say, Rohini isn't going to commit to a weekly Saket commute for one student. If your first-choice tutor is too far for home visits, online tutoring with the same person is almost always workable instead, and for Math AA HL specifically, a shared digital whiteboard handles the working-out just as well as a notebook does.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work for a subject as calculation-heavy as Math AA HL?
faqs.answer: For most students, yes, once the tutor uses proper tools - a shared digital whiteboard or tablet where working is written out step by step, not just talked through. What online tutoring can't fully replace is a tutor physically pointing at a specific line of algebra mid-mistake, which matters more for some learning styles than others. For Grade 12 students doing timed past-paper practice, online works especially well because screen-sharing a paper and marking it live is often clearer than marking on physical printouts during a home session.

faqs.question: What if there's no progress after a month?
faqs.answer: First, check whether 'no progress' means no grade change yet or genuinely no shift in understanding - grade movement often lags real comprehension by a few weeks. If the tutor can't point to one specific topic that's improved, that's the signal to act rather than wait another month. The options are a direct conversation about adjusting method, or a switch to a different tutor entirely. Neither is treated as a failure on the family's part; some combinations simply don't click, and that's addressed quickly.

faqs.question: How much does an IB Math AA HL tutor in Delhi cost?
faqs.answer: There's no single honest number here - it depends on the tutor's experience, whether sessions are home or online, and weekly hours needed. Tutors with strong HL-specific track records and IA mentoring experience sit at a higher rate than those newer to the syllabus, and home sessions in South Delhi typically cost more per hour than online ones. The practical approach: have the intake call first, get a quote tied to your requirement, then compare what's actually included - marking, IA feedback, between-session support - against the rate.

faqs.question: Can we switch tutors if it isn't working out?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it's a normal part of matching, not an admission something went wrong. A tutor excellent for a quiet, methodical student might be the wrong energy for one who needs faster pacing and direct correction. Give a new match two or three sessions before judging - the first is diagnostic and doesn't reflect steady-state teaching - but after that, if the fit still feels off, say so; a replacement is arranged, subject to availability. Fees for completed sessions aren't refunded, but nothing forces a family into a mismatch.

faqs.question: What does the first session actually cover?
faqs.answer: Not small talk - a diagnostic. The tutor works through a recent test, homework set or past paper with the student, watching where marks are lost: careless algebra, a misunderstood concept, weak exam technique under time pressure, or something else entirely. That diagnosis shapes the first month's plan, not a generic syllabus overview. Parents usually get a short summary afterward covering what the session revealed and what the next few weeks will focus on. Mention any upcoming school assessment before the first session so the tutor can prioritise around it.

faqs.question: How is Math IA support handled alongside regular tutoring?
faqs.answer: IA mentoring is usually folded into regular sessions rather than billed separately, though it depends on the plan agreed upfront. A tutor helps with topic selection first - something the student is genuinely curious about with enough mathematical depth for the criteria - then reviews drafts against IB's exploration and communication marking points, not just grammar. Delhi students juggling IA deadlines alongside school internal assessments and other coursework often need this scheduled a few weeks ahead of the school's own deadline, not the week before it's due.

faqs.question: Our school timings make evenings tight - can sessions work around that in Delhi traffic?
faqs.answer: This is one of the most common scheduling constraints in Delhi, and it's usually solvable but worth being upfront about. Online sessions handle it best, since there's no commute buffer needed and a 45-minute evening slot right after school activities is realistic. Home sessions need more lead time - a tutor travelling across the city during peak evening traffic may need built-in flexibility rather than a fixed 6pm start. Weekend sessions, either mode, are often where Delhi families end up finding the most reliable hour for deeper topics like calculus proofs.

introSummary: An IB Math AI HL tutor in Delhi does something a school teacher rarely has time for: sit with one student, find exactly where the Applications and Interpretation logic breaks down, and fix that gap before it becomes three more. Delhi's DP cohort splits between Math AA and AI, and AI HL trips up students who assume it's the easier option — it isn't, it's differently hard, heavy on modelling, technology and interpretation under exam pressure. IB Gram matches Delhi families with tutors who teach this exact syllabus, for home or online sessions across the city.

contentBlocks.heading: The Job a School Teacher Doesn't Have Time For
contentBlocks.body: A Math AI HL teacher in a Delhi international school is running a class of twenty-odd students through the same content, the same pace, the same due dates. That's the job, and it's a reasonable one — cover the Applications and Interpretation syllabus, mark the assignments, keep the batch on schedule for May or November exams. What that teacher cannot do is stop the whole class for forty minutes because one student never quite got the logic behind curve fitting or Voronoi diagrams. A tutor's job starts exactly where the classroom job stops. It means sitting with one student, working backward from where the confusion actually is — not where the syllabus says it should be by Grade 12 — and rebuilding from there. For AI HL, this matters more than families expect. The subject leans on technology, statistical modelling, financial mathematics and networks, and a student who is shaky on GDC use or misreads what a question is testing loses marks that have nothing to do with intelligence. Delhi adds its own layer: school timings, extracurricular commitments and traffic mean the tutoring plan has to fit around a schedule that's already full, not compete with it. A good match accounts for both the syllabus gap and the calendar reality.

Built around Delhi school timings and travel
Covers May 2026 and November 2026 exam sessions
Works alongside the school teacher, not instead of them

contentBlocks.heading: What Happens Before You Meet a Tutor
contentBlocks.body: Matching starts with specifics, not a general request for "a good tutor." We ask what the student is actually stuck on — Paper 1's non-calculator reasoning, Paper 2's technology-heavy modelling, or Paper 3's extended problem-solving — and whether the goal is catching up before a mock, working through the IA, or building toward May 2026 or November 2026. Grade, current predicted level, school (where the family is comfortable sharing it) and preferred mode all shape the shortlist. From there we suggest two or three tutors whose background actually fits: someone who has taught the Applications and Interpretation syllabus specifically, not just Math AA with the labels swapped, since the two courses diverge sharply after the first term. A first session is diagnostic rather than a straight teaching session — it's used to map what the student knows, what they've misunderstood, and how they work under time pressure. Parents get a plain read of where things stand, not a sales pitch dressed as feedback. From there scheduling is worked out around school hours, weekend availability and how much lead time exists before the next assessment. Tutor availability depends on subject, level and existing schedules, so a specific time slot isn't always guaranteed on the first try, and we say so upfront rather than overpromising.

Shortlist of 2-3 tutors matched to AI HL specifically
First session is diagnostic, not a sales pitch

contentBlocks.heading: Where AI HL Sits in the Wider IB Journey
contentBlocks.body: IB Gram supports the full run from the Primary Years Programme (ages 3 to 12) through the Middle Years Programme (ages 11 to 16) to the Diploma Programme (ages 16 to 19) — Grade 1 through Grade 12 across Delhi. AI HL only exists at the Diploma end, but the decision that lands a student there is usually made earlier, around Grade 10, when schools ask students to choose between Math AA and Math AI, then Standard versus Higher Level. That choice matters more than it gets credit for. A student strong in algebraic manipulation and abstract proof tends to do better in AA; a student who thinks in terms of real data, spreadsheets and applied problems is often better served by AI, and HL over SL only makes sense if the student is aiming at a course — engineering, economics, data science — that needs the depth. Where a student has already committed to AI HL and is finding it heavier than expected, a tutor's role shifts from "which path" to "how do we cover this path properly." That includes making sure the IA statistical investigation has a workable research question, that GDC and technology use is second nature by exam time, and that TOK and EE deadlines don't eat into revision weeks.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Sessions Where Travel Makes Sense, Online Where It Doesn't
contentBlocks.body: Home tutoring can be arranged in select South Delhi and central Delhi pockets — areas like Vasant Vihar, Greater Kailash, Saket and Chanakyapuri, plus nearby residential belts — where a tutor can reasonably reach the house without losing half the session to traffic. Outside those pockets, and for most of Delhi, online tutoring is the more realistic option, and for AI HL it often works better anyway: sessions can use a shared screen for GDC work, spreadsheet modelling and past-paper walkthroughs in a way that's easier than crowding around one laptop at a dining table. Many Delhi families end up choosing a hybrid pattern — home sessions when the subject needs sustained, in-person explanation and a specialist happens to be nearby, online when the priority is finding the right subject expert regardless of where they live in the city. Being honest about it: home tutoring in Delhi doesn't scale the way online does. Peak-hour traffic across South and Central Delhi can turn a 45-minute commute into 90, which is why the strongest AI HL tutors are often matched online even to families who would prefer someone at the door. The right question isn't "home or online" by default — it's which mode gets more focused hours in front of the syllabus each week.

contentBlocks.heading: The Subjects AI HL Students Usually Need Alongside It
contentBlocks.body: AI HL students rarely need help in isolation — the subject combination around it shapes how tutoring gets scheduled. In Delhi, the DP students working through Math AI HL are commonly also carrying Physics, Chemistry or Economics at HL, alongside English A and a language. A student doing AI HL and Physics HL together, for instance, benefits from a tutor who can point out where the statistics and modelling skills from AI actually show up in physics data analysis and uncertainty calculations — the syllabuses aren't taught as connected, but the skills are. Economics HL students lean on the same interpretation muscle AI HL builds: reading a dataset, drawing a defensible conclusion, showing working that would survive a moderator's scrutiny. English A, meanwhile, is where a lot of Delhi students lose time not because writing is weak but because time management across four HL subjects, IA deadlines and TOK essays collapses in Grade 12. A tutoring plan that only looks at Math AI HL in isolation misses this. The stronger approach maps a student's full subject load first, flags where deadlines cluster — mock season, IA submission windows, EE drafts — and builds the AI HL sessions around that reality rather than pretending the subject exists on its own.

Cross-subject skills: AI HL statistics feeding into Physics and Economics

contentBlocks.heading: Delhi Schools Whose DP Students We've Worked With
contentBlocks.body: Delhi's IB schools cluster around a few areas — Chanakyapuri and Saket carry a lot of the DP population — and tutors on IB Gram have worked with students from schools including The British School New Delhi, the American Embassy School and DPS International Saket. To be clear: IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform, not affiliated with these schools or with the IB Organization, and nothing here should be read as an endorsement from either side. What's useful about naming schools isn't credibility by association, it's that AI HL is taught with real variation between them — pacing, which technology is emphasised (GeoGebra versus spreadsheet-first approaches, for instance), how much class time goes to the IA versus content coverage, and how early mocks are scheduled. A tutor who has already seen a school's approach to AI HL, or at least a similar one, gets a student up to speed faster than one starting from a blank syllabus reading. For families at schools not listed here, that's fine too — the matching process asks about the school's pacing and past assessment style directly, rather than assuming every Delhi international school teaches AI HL the same way, because they don't.

contentBlocks.heading: South Delhi, Central Delhi and the Commute Math
contentBlocks.body: Home tutoring works best in a tight radius, and for AI HL that radius currently covers Vasant Vihar, Greater Kailash, Saket and Chanakyapuri, with reasonable stretch into Defence Colony, Hauz Khas, New Friends Colony, Panchsheel Park, Green Park and Jor Bagh — areas close enough together that a tutor can hold two or three sessions in an afternoon without the commute eating the value of the third one. Families slightly further out, in Gurugram, Noida or Ghaziabad, are better served by online sessions rather than a home tutor crossing NCR in evening traffic for a single hour — it's a two-hour round trip at minimum during peak time, and no amount of subject expertise makes up for a tutor who arrives exhausted or fifteen minutes late every week. Within South and Central Delhi itself, the areas above aren't interchangeable either: Chanakyapuri's diplomatic-zone traffic patterns differ from Saket's mall-and-market congestion, and a tutor who knows one route well may still find the other slow. This is why the platform asks for the actual address area early in matching rather than a general "South Delhi" tag — it changes which tutors are realistically available for home sessions, and how many can be offered before online becomes the more sensible recommendation.

contentBlocks.heading: Four Weeks In: What a Parent Should See
contentBlocks.body: A first AI HL session should leave a parent with something concrete: which papers the student is weakest on, whether the gap is conceptual or procedural, and a rough plan for the weeks before the next assessment — not vague reassurance that "we'll get there." By week two, sessions should be visibly working from that plan rather than restarting the diagnosis each time. By week four, there should be something measurable to look at: a past paper attempted under timed conditions, a specific topic that's moved from shaky to solid, or at minimum a clear, honest account of why progress is slower than hoped — a heavier-than-usual school workload, an IA that ate into revision time, or a foundational gap that needs another few sessions before the exam-focused work can begin. If a tutor isn't a good fit — teaching style clashes, pace is wrong for the student, or the subject depth turns out thinner than the profile suggested — that gets addressed directly rather than pushed through out of politeness. Switching tutors mid-plan isn't a failure of the process; continuing with a mismatch quietly is. Parents should expect a straightforward answer if they ask how their child is doing, not a diplomatic non-answer designed to keep the sessions going regardless of whether they're helping.

Weeks 2-3: sessions built around a concrete plan, not restarted diagnosis

contentBlocks.heading: How a Tutor Gets Listed for AI HL in the First Place
contentBlocks.body: Before a tutor is offered for AI HL, we check what they've actually taught and to what level — a mathematics degree alone doesn't tell you whether someone has handled the Applications and Interpretation syllabus specifically, which is different enough from Math AA that general "IB Maths" experience isn't a substitute. We look at subject background (the degree, plus any specific IB or DP teaching or tutoring history), familiarity with the current syllabus and assessment objectives, and whether they can talk through IA moderation criteria and Paper 3 problem-solving structure without hesitation, not just recite topic lists. There's a conversation before anyone gets listed — not a form filled in unsupervised — where we ask them to walk through how they'd approach a student who's weak on, say, the financial mathematics or the Voronoi diagrams / graph theory options. We don't publish star ratings or invented review counts, because a marketplace can't responsibly manufacture social proof it hasn't actually collected in a verifiable way; what we can vouch for is the screening itself and how a mismatch is corrected if one shows up in the first few sessions. Availability for any specific tutor still depends on their existing schedule and current student load, which is checked before, not after, they're recommended to a family.

faqs.question: Is Math AI HL actually easier than Math AA HL?
faqs.answer: No, and treating it that way is the most common mistake we see. AI HL trades abstract proof for statistical modelling, financial mathematics, networks and technology-heavy problem-solving under Paper 3's extended format. A student who finds algebra tedious but enjoys applied, data-driven problems will likely do better in AI than AA — but AI HL still demands real depth. It's a different kind of hard, not a lighter one, and tutors treat it that way from the first session.

faqs.question: How much does an IB Math AI HL tutor cost in Delhi?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the tutor's experience, whether sessions are home or online, and how many hours a week the plan needs — a once-weekly revision top-up costs less than an intensive plan rebuilding two years of gaps before May 2026. Home tutoring in South Delhi generally costs more than online because of travel time built into the tutor's rate. We share exact fees once we know the student's level and the shortlist of matching tutors, rather than quoting one number that doesn't reflect what any specific family would actually pay.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our home in Vasant Vihar or Greater Kailash?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes — Vasant Vihar and Greater Kailash sit inside the core area where home tutoring for AI HL is realistic, along with Saket, Chanakyapuri, Defence Colony and a few neighbouring pockets. Availability still depends on which tutors currently have capacity and how their schedule lines up with the family's preferred timing, so it isn't guaranteed for every request. If no home tutor fits the slot needed, online is offered as the alternative rather than leaving the family without an option while waiting for the right home match.

faqs.question: What does IA support for Math AI HL actually involve?
faqs.answer: It starts with the research question — a lot of IA marks are lost before any maths happens, because the question is too broad, too narrow, or not mathematical enough. A tutor helps narrow it to something the student can investigate with real data, then checks the mathematical processes are correct, sophisticated enough for HL, and clearly explained rather than just calculated. Feedback focuses on what a moderator checks against the criteria — not generic writing advice — since IA marks are lost more often on process and interpretation than on arithmetic.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work for a maths subject like this?
faqs.answer: For AI HL specifically, often better than expected, because so much of the subject is screen-based anyway — GDC work, spreadsheet modelling, graphing software. A shared digital whiteboard replaces the notebook, and past papers get marked up live on screen rather than passed back and forth. What online can't fully replace is a tutor physically checking handwritten working line by line, which matters more for younger students still building basic exam technique than for a Grade 12 student who already knows how to structure an answer under time pressure.

faqs.question: What happens if we're not happy with the tutor after a few sessions?
faqs.answer: Say so — that's the expected use of the process, not an awkward exception. We ask what specifically isn't working: pace, teaching style, subject depth, or scheduling friction, and use that to find a better-matched tutor rather than repeating the same mismatch. There's no penalty for switching and no pressure to justify it extensively. The only thing that helps is specifics, because "it's not working" alone doesn't tell us whether the next match should be slower-paced, more exam-focused, or simply a different personality fit for the student.

faqs.question: Our daughter is at DPS International Saket — do tutors already know that syllabus pacing?
faqs.answer: Some do, since DPS International Saket is one of the Delhi schools our tutors have worked with before, but the honest answer is it depends on which tutor is matched. What we confirm before the first session is the school's AI HL pacing, which topics have been covered, and when mocks are scheduled, rather than assuming last year's timeline still applies. If no tutor has direct DPS Saket experience, we prioritise one who has taught a comparable international school syllabus.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start if mocks are only a few weeks away?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but it changes what's realistic. A few weeks before mocks is enough time to consolidate weak topics, drill exam technique and fix careless errors that cost easy marks — it's not enough time to rebuild two years of foundational gaps from scratch. We'll say this plainly during matching rather than promising a turnaround that isn't credible: short-notice sessions focus on triage, identifying the highest-return topics first, with a longer-term plan discussed for after mocks if deeper gaps show up.

faqs.question: Do tutors help with TOK and the Extended Essay too, or only AI HL content?
faqs.answer: Primary focus is the subject requested, but many families ask the AI HL tutor to also glance at EE mentoring if the EE has a mathematical or data-driven angle, since it's the same skill set. TOK support is usually handled separately, often by a different tutor, because TOK's assessment style is different from mathematics and benefits from someone who teaches that specifically. We ask about all of it upfront during matching, rather than assuming one tutor should stretch across every DP requirement a student has.

heroSubtitle: For Grade 1 to Grade 12 students preparing for May 2026 or November 2026 exams, IB Gram matches Delhi families with Physics HL and SL tutors for IA planning, past-paper practice and mock revision, through home sessions in select South Delhi pockets or online tutoring anywhere in the city.
introSummary: Searching for an IB Physics tutor in Delhi usually means one of three things: your child needs steady HL or SL support, the IA is due and stuck, or mocks exposed gaps that need fixing before May 2026 or November 2026. IB Gram matches Delhi families across Grade 1 to Grade 12 with tutors screened for IB Physics specifically, not general science teaching. Home sessions are realistic in parts of South Delhi and central Delhi; everywhere else in the city, online tutoring is usually the more dependable choice, and often the stronger one anyway.

contentBlocks.heading: The first question to answer before you book anyone
contentBlocks.body:
Before you contact anyone, it helps to know which of three situations you are actually in. Some Delhi parents come looking for a Physics tutor because their child has just started Diploma Programme Physics and needs steady weekly support to keep pace with HL or SL content from week one. Others arrive because the Physics Internal Assessment is due in a matter of weeks and the student has a topic but no clear method. And a third group shows up after a mock exam, holding a Paper 2 script that lost marks not on concepts but on how answers were structured. Each of these needs a different kind of session, and a tutor who is good at one is not automatically good at the other two.

IB Gram works with students from Grade 1 to Grade 12, so a family can also start earlier, before Physics becomes high-stakes, if the goal is building comfort with problem-solving rather than exam technique. Support is planned around the May 2026 and November 2026 exam sessions, since a plan built four months out looks nothing like a plan built four weeks out. Delhi adds its own layer: schools run different calendars, students often commute across the city, and a tutor also needs to understand IB assessment expectations well enough to plan IA work, mock revision, past-paper practice, and where relevant, EE or TOK support, alongside regular subject teaching rather than instead of it.

contentBlocks.heading: Home sessions, online sessions, or a mix of both
contentBlocks.body:
Delhi is large enough that no single tutoring mode works for every family, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. Home tutoring can be considered in select South Delhi and central Delhi pockets, and in a handful of nearby residential areas where a tutor's travel time stays reasonable. Once you are further out, or on the wrong side of Delhi's traffic patterns at 5 pm on a weekday, home tutoring stops being a fair ask of anyone, tutor included. That is not a limitation IB Gram invented; it is how a city of this size actually works.

Online tutoring is available across the whole of Delhi, for every supported IB programme and subject, and for Physics specifically it works better than many parents expect. Diagrams, graphs and worked numericals all display clearly on screen, and a tutor can share past-paper questions in real time during a session rather than emailing them beforehand. Many Delhi families end up choosing a hybrid pattern deliberately: home sessions where travel is realistic and geography works in the family's favour, online sessions when a particular tutor's subject depth or timing availability matters more than proximity. A student preparing intensively before a mock, for instance, might want twice-weekly online sessions regardless of where the tutor is based, simply because that tutor's slot availability fits the school's revision calendar. The right mix usually depends on what stage the student is at, not on a fixed rule.

contentBlocks.heading: Where Physics fits alongside the rest of the Diploma workload
contentBlocks.body:
IB Physics rarely sits in isolation on a Delhi student's timetable. Most families booking a Physics tutor through IB Gram are also managing Math AA HL or Math AI HL, since Physics HL leans heavily on the calculus and vector work that Math AA covers, and a student weak in one visibly struggles in the other. Alongside Physics, Delhi students commonly need support in Chemistry, Economics and English A, either because the Diploma's six-subject spread leaves little slack for a struggling area, or because Physics is the subject exposing a gap that started in Math.

A Physics tutor working through IB Gram is expected to handle more than content delivery. That means IA planning specific to Physics, from choosing a researchable question to structuring data analysis with proper uncertainty treatment, since a vague or unoriginal Physics IA is one of the most common ways marks are lost. It also means being able to speak to EE mentoring where a student has chosen Physics for their Extended Essay, TOK support where a Physics example is being used to illustrate a knowledge question, and ordinary school assignment help between formal assessments. Mock revision and past-paper practice run throughout, since Physics Paper 1, Paper 2 and Paper 3 each test differently, and a student who has only practised Paper 2 style questions is underprepared for the data-response demands of Paper 3.

contentBlocks.heading: The Delhi pockets this actually covers

Home tutoring conversations through IB Gram most often start in Vasant Vihar, Greater Kailash, Saket and Chanakyapuri, where enough IB and international school families live close together that a tutor's travel time between sessions stays workable. Nearby pockets such as Defence Colony, Hauz Khas, New Friends Colony, Panchsheel Park, Green Park and Jor Bagh come up regularly too, and whether home tutoring makes sense there depends on the specific tutor's other commitments that week rather than a blanket yes or no.

Families in Gurugram, Noida and Ghaziabad also reach out, usually for the same reason: a strong Physics tutor is worth an online session even when a home visit is not realistic across that distance. This is where online tutoring genuinely outperforms home tutoring rather than merely substituting for it, since NCR traffic between, say, Saket and Gurugram at peak hours can eat more time than the session itself. A parent in Chanakyapuri weighing a home tutor against a strong online specialist in Physics HL should treat that as a real trade-off, not default to home tutoring out of habit. contentBlocks.heading: Physics changes shape from PYP science through the Diploma
contentBlocks.body:
IB Physics is not one fixed subject; what it asks of a student changes across the three programmes IB Gram supports. In the Primary Years Programme, covering ages 3 to 12, physics ideas show up inside broader units of inquiry rather than as a standalone subject, so a tutor's job is often about curiosity and observation skills rather than formal content. By the Middle Years Programme, ages 11 to 16, physics becomes a recognisable subject with its own assessment criteria, and a student starting to struggle here usually needs help connecting mathematical reasoning to physical concepts before the gap widens.

The jump to the Diploma Programme, ages 16 to 19, is where most tutoring requests concentrate, because Physics HL and SL bring formal assessment weight through Paper 1, Paper 2, Paper 3 and the Internal Assessment, on top of whatever TOK or EE commitments a student has taken on. A Delhi student moving from MYP Physics into DP Physics HL often underestimates how much more mathematical the HL syllabus becomes, and a tutor who taught them comfortably at MYP level may not be the right fit for HL mechanics and fields. This is a genuine limitation worth naming: continuity across programmes is nice when it works, but it should never come at the cost of matching a DP HL student with someone whose own strength was really at MYP level. IB Gram treats each transition as a point to re-check fit, not assume it.
items: PYP (ages 3 to 12): physics ideas inside inquiry units
MYP (ages 11 to 16): physics as a standalone assessed subject
DP (ages 16 to 19): Physics HL/SL with Paper 1-3 and the IA
MYP-to-DP HL jump is more mathematical than most students expect
Tutor fit is rechecked at each programme transition

contentBlocks.heading: How a match actually gets made
contentBlocks.body:
A request usually starts with a short description of where the student is: which programme, HL or SL, what triggered the search (steady support, an IA deadline, a mock result), and whether home or online is preferred. IB Gram uses that to shortlist tutors whose subject background and exam-board familiarity fit, rather than sending the first available person. For Physics specifically, that means checking whether a tutor has actually taught the HL syllabus's more mathematical units, not only SL-level content, since the two overlap less than their shared name suggests.

The first session is diagnostic rather than a straight launch into new content. A tutor typically reviews recent test or mock scripts, asks the student to work through a couple of problems live to see method rather than just the answer, and checks which Physics topics feel shaky versus which are genuinely misunderstood, two different problems that need different fixes. From there a short plan gets set, usually four to six weeks out, with a check-in point rather than an open-ended commitment.

By week four, a parent should be able to see something concrete: fewer careless errors in numerical answers, a clearer IA direction if that was the goal, or a specific, nameable topic that has improved on a follow-up test. If that is not visible, IB Gram treats it as a signal to look at the match itself, not to simply add more hours. Availability throughout this process depends on tutor schedules and is not something that can be promised in advance of an actual request.
items: Match is based on programme, level and reason for the search
HL Physics fit checked separately from SL fit
First session: diagnostic, not new content
Plan set for four to six weeks with a check-in
Week four: concrete, nameable evidence of progress expected

contentBlocks.heading: What gets checked before a tutor is recommended
contentBlocks.body:
Trust here is built on process, not adjectives. Before a Physics tutor is recommended to a Delhi family, IB Gram looks at their academic background in physics or a closely related field, their actual experience teaching the IB syllabus specifically rather than a generic Physics curriculum, and whether they have handled the assessment components that matter here: Paper 1 multiple-choice technique, Paper 2 and Paper 3 structured responses, and IA supervision. A tutor who has only taught school-board Physics can still be a strong teacher, but IB Physics has its own command terms, its own data-handling expectations and its own IA rubric, and that gap needs to be checked rather than assumed away.

None of this is expressed as a guarantee of a particular grade or score, because no honest tutoring platform can promise that, and any that does should be treated with suspicion. What IB Gram can be specific about is the process: what is checked before a match, what a first session is meant to establish, and what a parent should reasonably expect to see by a stated point in the plan. If a match is not working, the honest answer is to say so and adjust it, not to keep the family in a plan that is not producing anything while pretending otherwise. Subject to tutor availability, a family unhappy with a match can request a change, and that request is treated as useful information about fit rather than as a complaint to manage.
items: Academic background in physics or a related field checked first
Actual IB syllabus teaching experience, not generic Physics teaching
Paper 1-3 technique and IA supervision experience reviewed
No score or grade guarantees, ever
Mismatches are addressed directly, not smoothed over

contentBlocks.heading: Delhi's IB schools, and where IB Gram stands
contentBlocks.body:
Delhi's Diploma Programme families are often connected to a small set of schools, including The British School New Delhi and the American Embassy School, both in Chanakyapuri, and DPS International Saket. Students from these schools bring somewhat different starting points: an embassy-community student may have moved mid-programme from a different country's system, while a student at a long-established Delhi IB school may have followed the same cohort from MYP straight into DP. A tutor who understands these differences can calibrate faster instead of treating every DP Physics student as an identical starting point.

It needs to be said plainly: IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these or any other schools unless specifically stated. Nothing on this page should be read as a partnership, endorsement or access arrangement with The British School New Delhi, the American Embassy School, DPS International Saket, or the IB Organization itself. What IB Gram does is work alongside whatever a student's school is already teaching, filling gaps between school pace and individual understanding, supporting IA and EE work the school has assigned, and preparing for exam sessions the school has scheduled. A tutor's usefulness here comes from understanding IB Physics assessment structure in general and a given school's pacing and expectations in specific, and both matter: syllabus knowledge without knowing how a particular school actually tests it is only half the job.
